author: C Han
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | I flew with Emirates Taipei – Dubai – Geneva return. Outbound the onboard experience was a real nightmare. The flight attendants were arrogant and dismissive. Every time I tried to ask a question, they cut me off with clear impatience. I had to ask three times if I could try on the sunglasses I wanted to buy, and eventually had to stop an attendant again just to get a “no”. Then they simply forgot to bring me the product! One attendant was particularly rude — she was chatting with colleagues while ignoring my requests and even forbade me from crossing the galley to reach the restroom. The meal service was just as bad. They tried to take my tray before I had finished eating, and once I was done, no one ever came back. I was left stuck with my tray until the very last moments before landing. I couldn’t even fold my table or adjust my seat properly for arrival because the crew had completely abandoned me. On the return flight, the service was more normal. Some crew members were polite and even enthusiastic, which made the flight more pleasant. It wasn’t outstanding, but it was acceptable. Emirates used to be a great airline, but this experience left me very disappointed and  I will avoid flying with Emirates again.

author: S Hazim
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | Emirates failed to meet premium expectations due to uncomfortable economy seating, malfunctioning cabin equipment including broken entertainment screens and leaking air conditioning, and poor customer service. Despite excellent Indian vegetarian meals and kind cabin crew, the journey was marked by uncomfortably warm cabins, a chaotic boarding process, and a lack of response to a formal complaint.

author: Maria Betourne
review_text: Not Verified | My flight from Paris to Dubai was delayed over 10 hours, causing me to miss my connection. I had to fly out the next day, arriving more than 24 hours late. The hotel arranged in Dubai during the delay was appreciated but it's been the only positive part of this experience. As a Business Class passenger and Privilege Club member, I expected better. The disruption was bad, but the silence afterward made it worse. It's now been over two months. Despite repeated emails and calls, I'm still waiting for an apology on the compensation I'm owed under international regulations for delays over 6 hours (around €600) a free upgrade on my next traveling plan or even some free miles. Every time, I'm told Customer Affairs will respond within 30 days. That's never happened. At this point, it feels like I'm being strung along, and this has seriously shaken my confidence in Emirates as a loyal customer.

author: C Yeung
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | While the overall inflight service was quite unsatisfactory, the worst and most offensive part of my experience with Emirates was the Korean customer service call center - the two most unpleasant phone service experiences I have ever encountered in my life both happened with Emirates. ​I have been struggling for over a month with an unresolved mileage accrual issue. I called the center to get this sorted out, but from the very beginning, the agent continuously talked over me and interrupted me, making it completely impossible to hold a proper conversation. When this disruptive behavior repeated, I questioned the quality of their service, asking why the consultation was being handled this way. Shockingly, the agent falsely framed my legitimate complaint as "verbal abuse" and abruptly hung up on me. ​Hoping to speak with someone else, I called back immediately, but the exact same agent answered. When I requested to be transferred to a different representative, they simply told me to call back later. I called a third time, and once again, the same person picked up. ​Utterly frustrated, I stated that I wanted to officially escalate this issue and requested the agent's name. Incredibly, the agent refused to provide their name and told me to "solve it legally." It honestly felt like there was only one person running the entire Korean call center. When I asked how many employees were even working there since I kept getting connected to the exact same person, the agent repeatedly replied, "I cannot answer that." ​This is not an isolated incident. Even before boarding, when I called to inquire about the Business Class Chauffeur-drive service, the consultation was an absolute mess and deeply unpleasant. ​Emirates desperately needs to retrain and re-educate their phone agents. I have plenty of other complaints regarding their inflight service as well, but I will not even bother mentioning them because the behavior of this call center is, by far, the most unacceptable.

author: Thao Nguyen
review_text: Not Verified | I am writing to formally express my disappointment regarding our recent Emirates Business Class experience, which fell far below the standards expected. On 08 May, Emirates cancelled the Ho Chi Minh City – Boston flight for my mother and me without providing any explanation. Subsequently, our family’s return flight from Boston to Ho Chi Minh City on 20 May was also cancelled without notice, and Emirates changed the departure date to 23 May. Our travel agency contacted Emirates multiple times via email but received little to no response. When we requested to return on 21 May instead, Emirates informed us that only two seats were available, requiring one family member to fly separately on 22 May. However, seats on the 21 May flight still appeared to be available when checked independently. What was especially concerning was that Emirates requested an additional payment of approximately VND 40,000,000 for all family members to travel together on the same flight — despite the situation originating from Emirates’ own cancellations and schedule changes. Further issues occurred during our overnight transit in Dubai. Although all required entry documents had already been submitted via email in advance as attachment, our family was still asked to wait approximately two hours for approval. At the Dubai Connect counter, staff only then reviewed the previously submitted emails and requested that the documents be forwarded again before processing could continue. Overall, the repeated cancellations without explanation, lack of communication, inconsistent information, transit handling issues, and disappointing onboard service resulted in an experience far below reasonable expectations for Emirates Business Class passengers.

author: G Quade
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | The ground experience revealed troubling gaps in professionalism and respect that are difficult to ignore.  At Montréal–Trudeau (YUL), the ticket agents were engaged in casual conversation while passengers waited in line. When I reached the counter, the agent spoke to me in a curt manner and instructed me to drop my luggage at another location, without considering my business-class status nor the protocol affiliated with it. When I requested to speak with a supervisor, I was told there was no one available. The interaction felt dismissive and unprofessional. A few minutes later, another agent quietly stepped in and demonstrated a very different approach. He appeared to understand the appropriate procedures, reviewed my passport and ticket, and recognized the oversight. He apologized on behalf of his colleague, took charge of my luggage himself, and completed the check in with calm efficiency and respect. He then went a step further and personally escorted me to the one of the lounges. The return journey from Dubai to Montréal exposed a more serious issue. At the boarding gate in Dubai, I explained to the agent that my passport would not scan on the device and that it needed to be entered manually. Instead of acknowledging this and resolving the matter calmly, she abruptly snatched the passport from my hand and muttered, under her breath, a derogatory comment. Another passenger nearby heard the remark, intervened, and pointed out how disrespectful and inappropriate her behavior was, even suggesting that if she disliked her job, she should consider another line of work. Rather than de escalating, the agent began arguing with this passenger, all while I stood waiting for my passport to be processed. The entire interaction carried a sense of rude entitlement and left a lasting feeling of discomfort. The in flight service was polished, the cabin comfortable, and the food and beverage offerings wine, sparkling options, and spirits were of a good quality.
route: Montreal to Dar Es Salaam via Dubai

author: Natalia Vlasova
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   I had an Emirates flight from Bangkok to Da Nang, but I wasn't allowed on it. I panicked and bought an Emirates ticket at the airport because I wasn't allowed to board without a return ticket. Meanwhile, my friend, who was flying on a different airline, didn't encounter this requirement and checked in without any problems. I was planning to continue my journey by air, so I wanted a refund. I later learned that the refund fee for the Economy Saver fare was exorbitant, over 70% of the ticket price and I consider it a rip-off. It was a very unpleasant experience. I will never fly with Emirates again.

author: A Ivanov
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   The cabin temperature during the flight was extremely cold, to the point where it felt like a freezer. I asked the cabin crew for a blanket, but received an indifferent reaction. Nobody came back to assist me after my request, and I had to look for a flight attendant again to get any response.  I have flown with many airlines, but this was the first time I experienced such careless and indifferent treatment from airline staff. The plastic smiles of the flight attendants, the fake sweet talk — all of it felt like a facade.

author: S Naik
review_text: Not Verified | Like others, having a complete headache getting a refund due to the war. Everytime you speak to someone on Facebook (because its impossible to call them or use their live chat), you get a different answer as to what is going on. They are clearly working off a script because they cannot answer very specific basic questions. You also cannot speak to anyone in the mythical refunds team so there is no hope of a lot of us ever seeing our hard earned money again. Worst customer service ever.

author: Alina Chernousova
review_text: Not Verified | Due to the war situation in the Middle East, I cancelled my flights on April 1st. The hotel processed the refund immediately. Emirates, however, has not returned approximately 3000 EUR even after more than a month. On March 23rd, I was clearly informed that the refund would take up to 15 working days. That timeline has long passed. What followed has been particularly disappointing: multiple contacts with customer service, inconsistent information, and explanations that simply do not hold up — including being told I had not provided bank details (which is incorrect), followed by requests for “understanding” due to a high volume of refunds. One could perhaps understand delays. What is much harder to understand is the absence of transparency, accountability, and any sense of urgency in resolving a straightforward refund case.  For a company that positions itself as a leader in global aviation, this experience is surprising and not in a good way. At this point, I would hesitate to recommend Emirates to others.

author: Edward Quigley
review_text: Not Verified | I recently booked a flight with Emirates from Lisbon to Bali (booking reference LCFKW6). The original itinerary had a short 1h30 connection in Dubai, with a total travel time of around 19 hours. Prior to departure, we were only notified of a minor delay. At no point were we informed that this would result in a missed connection. Only at check-in, approximately 2.5 hours before departure, the passenger was told the onward flight had been changed, resulting in an 18-hour layover in Dubai and a total journey time of approximately 36 hours. Had this been communicated earlier, alternative arrangements could have been made. We were instructed to seek assistance at the transfer desk in Dubai, but no hotel, lounge access, or meaningful support was provided despite the extended layover. This represents both a failure of communication and a lack of duty of care. The significantly extended transit time also created additional stress and concern, as a short connection had been specifically chosen in light of the broader regional situation. Overall, a very disappointing experience.

author: E Pan
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   I conclude that they are truly worse than a budget carrier. I received a horrendous customer service on-board flight by a cabin supervisor who was unable to manage a difficult passenger sitting on the other end of my row who was trying to take a nap at 5pm, so he came up to me to command me to close the window shades. I explained to him I was feeling unwell and wanted to leave it slightly open (1/4 open and 3/4 closed). He refused! He said that there’s another passenger across the aisle that is complaining and I should comply with his request. Only when I ask him if I fainted on board, would he be responsible, did he say it was my right to leave the window shades open and he will handle it with that lady. Many people had their window shades opened. Mine was three quarter 3/4 closed. Does it make sense that instead of forcing me, he should have given her an eye mask instead?  Inefficiency of Customer Service Team with replies almost only once a month. Upon arrival, I noticed damage made to my luggage. My flight landed in Singapore on 29 Dec 2025, I wrote in on 29 Dec 2025, received one reply on 29 Jan 2026 and the next reply on 23 Feb 2026 with only a partial reply on both emails. I asked the customer service staff Najma a simple question 5 times but up till the end of March 2026, I am still unable to get a refund or an answer.

author: Paul Bailey
review_text: Not Verified | Flew in business class from Hong Kong to Bangkok on the 20th March. The lounge at Hong kong airport was nowhere near to Emirates usual standard. The aircraft looked very dated indeed with sockets for the TV not working and neither were the USB sockets for charging our phones. The seats were extremely uncomfortable for a business class flight Food was average at best and service was also very slow. A passenger who spent most of the journey at the on-board bar was drunk when he returned to his seat. Even although the same passenger became rather loud and was also stood up in the aisle just after landing the crew did nothing about the passengers behaviour. This is not acceptable.

author: Michael Schade
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | Check in at BKK was a breeze, lounge with a good choice of F&B. Boarding well organised. The upgraded seats on their A380 are spacious, more comfortable and private. The entertainment system has the best choice, screen size and responsive. Complimentary WIFI worked well throughout the flight. Service was good, beverages of high quality; food was nothing to write home about. The flight from DXB was very different. A rather tired looking and noisy B773 with the old angled flat 2-3-2 configuration. The seats were just ok for the day-flight, but not acceptable for a nightlight. Food was rather underwhelming and service sloppy. I had to make the same requests for drinks and amenities up to three times. No amenity kits for both flights (7 and 8 hours) ,both flights on time. What was missing here was consistency; with one great flight, and the next with below average hard and soft products,

author: T Roseby
review_text: Not Verified |  I am very disappointed with Emirates. I booked my tickets almost a year before travelling as I like to carefully select my seat and more importantly, the type of aircraft I will be travelling on. Emirates changed the second half of the inbound journey from an A380(which I had booked) to a 777-300. They did not even inform me. I found out when I was looking something up, which resulted in me phoning them and writing to them to ask to move me back to any A380 going into any London airport at any time that day. My e-mail, I never got a reply to, and the telephone conversation resulted in them saying I could pay an additional £400,- for the honour of changing my ticket due to what they had done, not me. They later put a disclaimer on the booking saying “mixed fleet”. The 777-300 was an old and noisy aircraft with an illuminated Non Smoking sign above my head, and nowhere to put my bag anywhere near me. To me, it felt more like a Premium Economy than business class. I have flown with Emirates many times, and I booked the A380 for a reason. Buyer beware.

author: T Maddern
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Business Check-in was a bit of a trek from the metro station, but I appreciated the priority tags and also my ski bag being taken from the check-in counter, rather than me having to drag it to the other side of the terminal. Emirates have organised their lounges so they're above the gate you leave from. The lounge had a good array of foods for breakfast. I was pretty annoyed that they didn't give us a jetbridge to board, but bus instead.  On board the crew spoilt us, meals were beautifully presented and they tasted great and there was an array of snacks available. The seats were not the refurbished seats, but were still very comfortable. The cabin was only about 1/2 full, so plenty of room to move around. We were delayed in immigration at Denpasar due to me not following the correct procedure with the airport tax and our bags were waiting for us at the carousel. I'll definitely give Emirates another go.

author: Martin Greenwood
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   I sometimes wonder of the veracity of some over praiseworthy reviews, or were we just unlucky? Our our Manchester to Dubai flight business class was atrocious, we were stuck in the middle two of three centre business class seats - most airlines premium economy is better than this, and the plane was tired and fixtures worn and tatty. Service was abrupt and staff disappeared into the kitchens and stayed there for most of the flight. The food was okay, at BA standard from my recent trips with them. Luckily our transfer in Dubai was fairly brief, because it is an awful place. Our trip in April to Thailand is with Qatar Airways, who are a very long way ahead of Emirates in my experience - a bit like comparing Waitrose with Lidl.

author: Peter Dyson
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | The flights in Business class were full but the crew were excellent and attentive. The food on the Dubai to Birmingham flight was excellent, a starter of prawn, scallop and fennel and main of trout. Excellent service which must be down to the Cabin Managers who have my compliments

author: John Rolfe
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |  Check in at Colombo was quick and there is a priority immigration queue at Colombo that saves a bit of time. Emirates Lounge is of a decent size and is comfortable, with a reasonable choice of food. Flight to Dubai was on a refurbished B777 with the new seating, very comfortable. We chose the smoked salmon starter and roast chicken as the main, genuinely nice. Flight had Wi-Fi onboard but not the latest StarLink and service was a bit unstable. Due to congestion we were 45 minutes late into Dubai. This meant a very tight transit in Dubai. At the time of booking our trip the leg from Dubai to London Gatwick was on an A380, unfortunately Emirates changed the aircraft to a B777 two weeks before travel but did not have the courtesy to advise the passengers, This aircraft was the older config B777 (some 20 years old) with the 3 seats in the middle business class. Whilst I understand Emirates right to change the aircraft type, this was a big step down compared with our expectation of comfort and service, which we had paid for. Their failure to communicate the change was disappointing. The disappointment didn’t end there as the aircraft then suffered a recurring technical issue, which meant the flight was almost 4 hours late departing and almost 3 hours late arriving into Gatwick. These things happen and you must accept this, however frustrating! The service provided by the crew was brilliant and whilst we were on the ground and we got airborne, they were very attentive and the meal and drink service was very good.

author: John Rolfe
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |  Check in at LGW was quick and easy. Flight to Dubai was on an A380, which we prefer to the B777. My wife and I had seats 9E and 9F, which are the middle ‘honeymoon’ seats!. Service was very slick with a good cabin crew. We both chose the beef fillet as the main course, which was tender and juicy. Flight was uneventful with no turbulence. Toilets kept clean and nice to enjoy the bar at the rear of the cabin. Flight landed ahead of schedule. Transit through Dubai was easy with minimal queuing at Transit security. Connecting flight from Dubai to Colombo was on a refurbished B777. We had seats 5E and 5F, very comfortable and the overall ambience on the cabin was very nice. Aircraft was fitted with StarLink so super stable and free Wi-Fi available, very impressive. Flight was only 4 hours, so we didn’t bother with the cooked breakfast offered, so just had the fruits and pastries prior to landing on Colombo. Flight arrived slightly ahead of schedule, immigration was quick and the bags were already on the belt! Overall, very good job by Emirates.

author: Irfan Awan
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |  Extremely disappointing experience on Emirates EK416 (Dubai to Sydney, 06 Feb — 13h 50m flight). Despite booking my family under a single booking reference, Emirates split us across different rows, seating my wife and one child separately from me and my other child. Another passenger was placed in our original aisle seats, forcing our family apart on a nearly 14-hour long-haul flight. It looks like Emirates is deliberately separating families to push passengers into paying extra for seat reservations. This is unethical, customer-unfriendly, and unacceptable, especially when traveling with children. Family seating should be a basic right, not a paid privilege. This experience has seriously damaged my trust in Emirates.

author: B Fan
review_text: Not Verified |  Only one of the legs the plane was an A380. Decent legroom for economy, plane was in small sections with additional restrooms. Much better design than the Boeing 777s which I had to endure for 3 of the legs with horrible leg room for long haul flights. Decent options for meals and efficient service. Check-in process efficient. Did not provide notification that flight was canceled from DXB - IAD. the status showed my flight was one time (It was not!) I had to go to the app and look at updates. Only happened to see 1-2 days later and scrambled to re-book. They gave me a really bad connection which increased my journey by 14+ hrs. I had paid for aisle seats but they put me in the window and aisle seats which is a rip-off. However, due to my insistence they did give me hotel for my 10 hr layover in DXB which was handled efficiently. It was a mixed bag. I can't honestly say it's a top tier airline. Middle of the pack. Not sure I will use again.

author: J Carter
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   I have to use this airline regularly when travelling to Dubai, as I have no real alternative. The aircraft are very large, which makes boarding and disembarkation particularly time-consuming. The level of service is often below expectations. In short, it is overrated.

author: N Pardahit
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   My wife and I flew from Boston to Delhi and back in the newly reconfigured 777 Business class. The seats, layout, water availability, entertainment options were good. We found the service in Emirates to vary widely. We are convinced this is due to the crew we have on the flight. The journey to Delhi on both flights was terrific. The staff was attentive, served the meals on time, took extra care of my wife who is hard of hearing. Unfortunately the return journey from Dubai to Boston was terrible. Both my wife and I felt the service was lacking the care, the food quality was poor and missing personalized attention. It looked as if the crew were performing the service from a check list. This was a poor flight experience. It left a sour taste and we will consider other airlines for future travel.

author: Aaliyan Shahzad
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   The crew was the best part of the flight. The plane had scratched windows, old/outdated screens, and the touch didn’t even work. The whole cabin felt worn-out.

author: Ralph Jones
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   It’s been a while since I have seen such poor service. Crew looked uninterested and many were inexperienced. One senior had a group of four crew members together to give detailed instructions of service in economy class. A very slow food service. Still serving the last of the economy meals over Bahrain, around one hour before landing into Dubai.  Call bell went unanswered for around 7 to 8 minutes.

author: N Kumar
review_text: Not Verified |  I was very disappointed with my recent experience flying with Emirates. The pre-boarding process was extremely disorganized. Cabin crew appeared uncoordinated and were running around without clear direction, which set a poor tone from the start of the journey. During meal service, my pre-requested vegetarian meal, which I had arranged several weeks prior to the flight, was not provided. This is a basic expectation on long-haul flights and reflects poorly on the airline’s attention to detail and passenger needs. The speed and efficiency of service throughout the flight was also subpar. Service was slow, inconsistent, and highlighted the lack of organization among staff. Additionally, Emirates often promotes its ICE entertainment system as industry leading, but I found the movie and TV selection to be outdated and underwhelming. Overall, this flight fell well below expectations. I would only consider flying with Emirates again if there were no other options, as there are several airlines offering comparable—or better—service at a lower cost.

author: Timothy Patrick
review_text: Not Verified |    Great service from Salma in PE. The ground service was awful and I would not recommend this route to anyone. check in at Bogotá - we waited 2 hours in a slow line . No priority for Dubai pax or premium economy. Worst experience I’ve had in 20 years of flying. One uniformed staff member who strutted around but no eye contact with any passengers. No line management . Miami arrival - after immigration (there is a transit line but it’s not clear) baggage was shambolic . Dubai bags came out last. Took around an hour, no priority label given. Gate far away. Again on board all great. Guys at transit desk work very slowly with no urgency. Crew saw the luggage shambles and wisely left the airport quickly . Based on the appalling ground service I’d avoid this route. Do not recommend.

author: Karim Boulos
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Worst service on flight I had. Internet wouldn’t work at all although constantly refreshing. They also didn’t accept to refund the amount they charged. They also delayed us 2 hours and half to leave and barely offered us any top ups for wine.

author: A Raneri
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   This review was being written while passengers are still on a bus, driving for more than ten minutes to reach the aircraft. Over multiple flights, a clear and uncomfortable pattern has emerged: routes serving certain countries are repeatedly assigned remote gates with bus boarding, while flights to other destinations receive jet bridges. When this happens again and again, it no longer feels like an operational coincidence — it feels like unequal treatment based on route, and by extension, the passengers traveling on it. Adding to the frustration is the behavior of some ground staff. Instead of empathy or professionalism, passengers are often met with impatience and dismissive attitudes, which only reinforces the feeling of being treated as less important.  Equal standards should apply to all passengers, regardless of where they are flying to. Respect, fairness, and consistency are not optional values.

author: John White
review_text: Not Verified |    One of the worst customer service experiences I’ve ever had. I have been trying to have miles credited from a completed international trip for over five months. During this time, I have called the Emirates call centre at least five times. On every occasion, I was told the issue would be resolved within 48 hours. Not once did anything happen. Instead, I was repeatedly bounced between Emirates and Qantas, each airline claiming the other was responsible. No ownership. No accountability. No resolution. Just endless deflection. The call centre experience has been exceptionally poor. Agents provide scripted responses, make promises they clearly cannot keep, and then disappear behind another “48-hour” timeline that means absolutely nothing. Escalations go nowhere. Follow-ups are ignored. You are left feeling completely powerless as a customer. This level of incompetence is shocking for an airline that markets itself as premium. If this is how Emirates handles something as basic as loyalty points, I shudder to think how genuine operational issues are managed. To make matters worse, this experience comes on top of frustrating connecting-flight coordination and a total lack of joined-up service across partner airlines. The entire system feels fragmented, outdated, and indifferent to the customer. After months of wasted time, repeated calls, and zero progress, I have lost confidence not just in Emirates Skywards, but in Emirates as a brand. This is not a premium airline experience. It is bureaucracy, deflection, and silence. I would strongly caution anyone who values their time, loyalty, or sanity.

author: S Hales
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | EK241 was a complete disaster from start to finish. My wife and I purchased companion seats with extra leg room (67H/J) only to have the experience ruined by an unruly tour group and kids who made going back and forth to the bathroom a group activity. When the issue was raised with the Cabin supervisor at the end of the flight, he placed the onus on us to communicate the issue, despite me countering that the cabin supervisor has a responsibility to manage the cabin by regularly walking around the cabin. Sorry Emirates, slick advertising does not translate into value added for the customer.

author: Timothy Patrick
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Hong Kong check in unfriendly and brusque. Staff added the dreaded SSSS to my ticket which got me enhanced check in Dubai - not fun. On board staff seemed frenetic and not super friendly. Cabin way too warm. Dubai stop all ok and then the long flight to Miami. The crew were wonderful. Food drinks super and seat great. Stop in Miami a bit stressful. You recollect bag and then add it to a special desk and do slow security. Flight to Bogotá great, quiet business class and lovely staff.
route: Hong Kong to Bogotá via Miami

author: M Halsten
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Emirates used to be a great Airline but that was many years ago. I always enjoyed flying with them and the service was great. Nowadays the airplanes are old, technical equipment is outdated and they are getting more strict with luggage. Every month I’m only traveling with hand luggage and a small backpack with laptop to save time when arriving. I have a tense timeline in dubai and cannot afford to lose time. Anyway, they told me to have my hand luggage being checked in and there was no chance to put it into the airplane - not even with extra payment. This doesn’t even happen with discount airlines but a premium airline is acting this way. Next time I’ll go with different airline to be sure not to miss any meetings.

author: Ron Earnshaw
review_text: Not Verified |  The worst flight I've been on. Poor service from the cabin crew, children screaming, and a terrible off duty Emirates employee on the flight being a real jerk. Their complaint system is onerous, and Emirates did nothing about the entire situation.

author: Mayanka Khetarpal
review_text: Not Verified |  I was disappointed with the airline. The aircraft & seats from Bombay to Dubai were very uncomfortable. Food served on that sector was very average & disappointing. The service from Dubai to Nice was very slow, the first meal was served an hour and a half after take off and we barely finished the first meal and we were given the second meal in an hour after we finished the first . On the way back the food from Dubai to Bombay was very average. Overall I was not very satisfied with flying Emirates.

author: Hasantha Gunasekera
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |    New aircraft and good service for this short haul fllght. Seat was good and food not too bad. Service OK. Was able to access First Class Lounge as Oneworld Emerald - a huge lounge with multiple food and entertainment options.

author: Hasantha Gunasekera
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   This is truly a great experience and well worth using Frequent Flyer points to upgrade! With the Dom and Caviar and 5 minute shower in the air, it is the definition of luxury. The suite is spacious and there are multiple snack options right at your seat, without having to call anyone, while watching the huge selection of entertainment options. I couldnt find Ghosts (UK version) on this flight (but it was on the short haul route from Bahrain), so it seems the options vary by flight. The crew was exceptionally friendly and helpful - very different to the Emirates general Ground staff (other than the First Class Checkin and Lounge staff), who I have found to be rude and disinterested on multiple occasions over decades, including this trip. Sad, but at least the in flight crew are great.

author: N Barsal
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |    Horrible lounge at Miami with filthy bathrooms terrible food. Disappointing business class with inconsistent service and poor food selection. Small bathrooms and unclean at times.

author: N Reddy
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | I had the worst experience with the Emirates baggage customer care team. My luggage was lost during travel, and instead of proper support, the compensation process was extremely disappointing. I lost around 12 kg of personal items including clothes, shoes, and essential belongings. Emirates is asking for original purchase receipts for compensation, which is not realistic. No one travels assuming their luggage will be lost and keeps receipts for everything they pack. The compensation offered was very low and not even close to the value of what I lost. Even buying a single pair of good shoes with it is difficult. On top of that, the process is extremely slow. It took almost a month just to get an update, and now the compensation payment is said to take another month. This entire process has been stressful, time-consuming, and disappointing.

author: C Heale
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   The last leg from Dubai to Phuket was a very disappointing experience. Seats are narrow, recline was limited. Hospitality was nothing great so for us this was the last time flying Emirates. The premium price is not getting you any better service, seats or boarding service.

author: F Carter
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |    They are not accommodating at all — especially when it comes to their call centre. I fly with Emirates around four times a year because I have to travel through Dubai, but if I could avoid them, I certainly would. I honestly don’t understand where their so-called good reputation comes from. I’m a frequent traveller, flying both economy and business class several times a year with airlines such as Thai Airways, Cathay Pacific, Turkish Airlines, Ethiopian Airlines, and Singapore Airlines — and all of them are better than Emirates. It’s hard to comprehend how Emirates is so overrated. And this opinion isn’t based on one bad experience — it has happened many times. Not to mention delays, cancellations (including one from Antananarivo), and overall poor service. Simply awful.

author: Azqan Baig
review_text: Not Verified | I travelled with Emirates on flight EK087 from Dubai to Zurich on 29 October 2025, and my experience has been extremely disappointing. My checked-in luggage was left behind in Dubai. The supervisor at Dubai Airport assured me it would be sent on the next available flight and delivered directly to my hotel in Zurich — but that promise was never fulfilled. This was an important business trip, and all my business suits, documents, and personal essentials were in my luggage. Because of the delay, I suffered serious inconvenience and financial loss, including the cancellation of a business meeting. It has now been three days, and I have still not received any update or information from Emirates. I have contacted customer service more than 20 times through calls and chats, and each time I was promised a follow-up — yet no one ever contacted me. The lack of responsibility, communication, and empathy from an airline of this reputation is truly unacceptable. I am now seeking compensation for the financial and personal losses I have suffered, and I sincerely hope Emirates handles this matter with the seriousness it deserves.

author: H massin-
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |  While checking in from Dubai to Dhaka, I had one hand carry bag which had only 6 KG weight. The check in counter agent forcefully gave my carry bag to booking even though I had requested him not to because I had Laptop in it. He denied and he didn't even look at to my eyes while interacting, keep on looking to the monitor and said "It is rule" he can't do anything. I didn't expect this type of service from Emirates.

author: Stacey Del Socorro
review_text: Not Verified | Our flight from London was delayed, and we were stranded in Dubai two days. The airline provided hotel accommodation and returned our checked luggage, which had already been weighed and confirmed within the baggage limit. The evening we were about to leave, during check-in for our flight to the Philippines, things took a negative turn. The baggage counter staff member or manager seemed surprised that I spoke fluent English and kept asking, “Are you Filipino? Where did you learn English?” The repeated questioning felt uncomfortable and unnecessary. When he checked our luggage again, he suddenly said it was overweight, even though it had been approved earlier. My mother was anxious about missing the flight, so we complied. But he kept lecturing “you need to understand the English ruels more on weight for bags.” Even when my bag showed 30.2 kg, well within the usual 1–2 kg leeway, he insisted I remove items. Some of my packed food from London was confiscated without clear explanation. Overall, it was an embarrassing and disappointing experience. The inconsistency in baggage handling made us feel disrespected.

author: J Foster
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | There was a long queue, even in business class — I was flying business. Boarding these enormous aircraft is always a challenge, as there are never enough ground staff or air bridges. Not to mention the economy passengers who must queue for nearly a hundred metres before reaching their seats. My previous flight was with Air Mauritius, a smaller airline, but there were only a handful of passengers in business class and I felt much more comfortable. Emirates, on the other hand, is really about the mass market. It doesn’t offer the same refined, intimate luxury experience I’ve had with some other airlines. The aircraft are always full, and overbooking is common — I’ve even been bumped to another flight before because of it. That said, the onboard service was perfectly fine. Emirates is widely praised — though not by me — and I find it somewhat overrated. It’s all about moving as many people as possible; the goal is clearly to fill those massive planes, and it shows. Unfortunately, this comes at the expense of true quality. I will fly with them again as I have to on some routes but I have not been impressed by Emirates since before Covid.

author: Wayne Good
review_text: Not Verified |    Geneva to Dubai I was able to upgrade with points to Business. Newly refitted 777 with 1-2-1 seating. Very nice, although the armrests are fixed so narrows the sleeping position a bit. The screen is enormous. Food excellent and food very good. Lovely service. Being Skywards Gold I love how the purser always personally welcome me. Remote stand in Dubai. This puzzles me as there were plenty of air bridges available. Good 4 hour layover in Dubai lounge. Dubai to Auckland, plane packed, so no upgrades available. As far as economy goes, Emirates does it well, however they can’t help crying children. And there were 2 very near me. I was silly not having any ear plugs with me. I usually sleep, even in economy, but not really able to. A very long 16 hours, leaving me quite tired. Food was very good, good service. Was very pleased to get off in Auckland. Which leads me to something else. Why oh why does it take so long for the air bridge to be attached to the plane in Auckland. After such a long flight all you want to do is get off. A good 20 minutes! Happens all the time in Auckland. So good flights.

author: Hairil Fahmi Yusof
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |  I recently flew with Emirates and had a mixed experience. The plane felt quite old and narrow compared to expectations, which made the journey less comfortable. Not very wheelchair-friendly overall, though some effort was made. The meals served were enjoyable, and the toilets were well maintained throughout the flight. The crew were friendly and patient, especially in accommodating my mother who was traveling in a wheelchair. However, their grooming standards could be improved — some did not appear as neat or polished, with hair not properly combed. Overall, while the food and cleanliness met expectations and the crew were kind, the aging aircraft, limited accessibility, and grooming standards left room for improvement.
route: kuala Lumpur to Jeddah via Dubai

author: Ken Howie
review_text: Not Verified | The Emirates chauffeur service is superb, and check-in was quick and easy. However it was quite a trek to the lounge, and not well signposted. Boarding was a breeze, direct from the lounge. The A380 cannot be faulted, and is matched by the attitude of the crew. Meal service was quite slow, particularly taking into account the time and duration of the flight. I decided I had to experience the onboard bar, a first time, which would be great on a long flight. In Dubai I had requested assistance, which was fortunate as it was a considerable distance to another terminal. Again boarding was direct from the lounge, and instead of the old 777 with 2x3x2 configuration, it was the new version with same seating as the A380. What an improvement. On arrival in Durban I was through passport control, had my luggage, met my chauffeur, and was on my way to the car within 30 minutes. All in all this was an excellent trip in both directions, the chauffeur service being the cherry on the top.

author: S Manhein
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Entering the A380 give you that feeling wow. Stunning design, smiling cabin staff with a tray of drinks. The menu is out of quality paper and warm towels are served. Staff introduce themselves and are so attentive through the trip. My food is beautiful. I enjoyed Grey goose.

author: M Basari
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   I am extremely disappointed with Emirates. I entrusted my baggage to them, even paid an additional $230 for excess luggage, and yet they managed to lose it. It has now been 8 days, and my baggage is still missing with no concrete update. At Vancouver Airport, under the supervision of the airport information desk, I contacted Emirates. After spending a very long time on hold and explaining the situation to the first operator, I was transferred to a second person—only to repeat my story again—who then transferred me to a third representative. This last individual was shockingly rude and dismissive, completely unprofessional for an airline that promotes itself as “luxury.” He bluntly told me that he would not help me and that everything must be done online, despite the fact that I had already completed the online process multiple times. This experience has completely destroyed the positive image I once had of Emirates. For an airline that prides itself on premium service, their handling of my baggage situation and customer support has been nothing short of unacceptable. I will think twice before flying with Emirates again.

author: Franz Larsen
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |  The service, the food even the cleaness of the planes has drastically degraded since cCovid. I used to look forward to fly with this company now I also try to find an alternative. Sad to see what used to be a prominent brand become just another common airline.

author: N Su
review_text: Not Verified | This was my first time flying with Emirates, and I expected better. With all the hype around them being a world-class airline, I figured I was in good hands. Turns out, I was wrong. I flew from Bangkok to Dubai, then on to Amsterdam. Things got rocky during landing in Dubai—literally. The plane hit serious turbulence, and just seconds before touching down, the pilot suddenly pulled up and went around again. Total chaos onboard. People were panicking, and the woman next to me went into a full-blown panic attack. We were left in the dark for a while until the captain finally announced, 15 minutes later, that we couldn’t land due to strong winds. Fair enough but say something sooner. The silence made everything worse. When we finally landed, I had just 30 minutes to catch my next flight. There were zero ground staff around to help. No signs, no directions, nothing. I had to full-on sprint across Dubai airport just to barely make it. At the gate, staff casually told me, “You’re really late, we were about to leave.” I told them my flight was delayed and they just said, “But you made it!”  Zero accountability. On the next leg to Amsterdam, I pushed the call button because I needed water to take my meds (window seat, couldn’t easily get up). Nothing. I waited over two hours. Not a single crew member showed up. I only got water when food was finally served. Three hours in, someone came by and noticed the call light still on. I told them I pressed it ages ago. They just said, “Okay, please turn it off then.” That’s it. No apology, no acknowledgment, nothing. Honestly, no one gave a damn. I’ve flown with over 20 airlines (yes, mostly economy), and this was hands down one of the worst experiences I’ve had. Not because of the turbulence, that happens. But the way Emirates handled everything? A complete joke.

author: Val Marques
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   The flight was good, no problems, however, they damaged my baggage. When I filed the complaint, the customer service representative tried to wiggle out every single possible reason not to assume the responsibilty. First he claimed I didn't lodge the claim within specified timeslot. Overturned. I proved to him I did lodge it on time. Then he claimed that I didn't pack the luggage correctly. Overturned - if they accepted it to be carried as check in luggage, then it was packed to their standards. When he run out of options, he just stated that he considers this matter closed and no furter action will be taken. That's it. No dispute resolution process. So effectively, I left with crushed luggage and no compensation. Take your luggage with you if you don't want it to be used as a trampoline by the baggage handlers

author: Virginia Bolton
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Recently flew Emirates Business class for the first time. The crew between Melbourne and Dubai is the best crew I have experienced, and the crew between Dubai to Munich were excellent as well. The flights were comfortable on the A380, my favourite aircraft. However the fit out is starting to look a bit tired, but the seats were reasonably comfortable (although have travelled in better on other airlines). The armrests seem to be the wrong height. It was different but I got used to it The meals and service were fantastic. And the wifi worked. The entertainment system is excellent - caught up on some movies. Landing in Munich, I was through customs and had collected my bag within 15 minutes.. that’s a record for me. Also enjoyed the chauffeur service.

author: Frederik Botha
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |  Cairo to Bangkok via Dubai to Bangkok. What is usually a very taxing and boring flight, was made immensely more enjoyable on Emirates! The staff pay diligent attention to passengers, the cleanliness of the plane and WC's, the nice touch of supplying a snack or two when asking for water, all this makes this a very enjoyable flight. And of course the in-flight Entertainment System is top-notch. A Flight Attendant came round offering to take an instant photo as a memento of my flight, haven't ever experienced this.

author: S Yan
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |  I am utterly disappointed with Emirates and feel completely misled after two consecutive nightmare experiences. My first flight was booked from Hong Kong to NYC with a stated layover in Dubai. Upon checking in, I was shocked to discover an additional layover in Milan. This was never mentioned at any point during the booking process. I specifically paid a premium for a one-stop flight, not two. Other two-stop flights were cheaper, but Emirates charged me more and delivered an inferior, longer product. The return trip from Rio to HK was even worse. After Dubai, the plane landed in Bangkok for 1.5 hours. We were held on the hot aircraft without being allowed to disembark. When I politely asked to get off to use the WiFi and stretch my legs, I was refused. Upon returning to my seat after this ordeal, I discovered that the cleaning crew had already removed all my personal belongings. While the staff retrieved my jacket, my wash bag and original cables were lost forever. Their "solution" was to hand me a bunch of random, mismatched cables. I strongly advise anyone booking a flight to avoid Emirates unless you enjoy paying for a premium product and receiving a substandard, deceptive service.
route: Rio De Janeiro to Hong Kong via Dubai / Bangkok

author: James Saks
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | We pre-booked a bassinet with Emirates well in advance, specifically for our one-year-old, only to be told onboard that he could not fit in it. Instead of offering a practical solution, the staff’s response was to push us into paying for an upgrade to a larger seat — while my wife was forced to sit with the baby strapped to her for the entire flight. At no point during booking or pre-departure was the bassinet’s actual size or weight limit communicated. Had we known, we would have booked our child his own seat with a car seat from the start. This lack of transparency caused unnecessary stress and discomfort on a long-haul journey. To make matters worse, the crew we dealt with were rude, dismissive, and showed no genuine willingness to help a family traveling with an infant. Their attitude made a difficult situation even more unpleasant. Strongly advise against flying with Emirates if you’re traveling with a baby — especially if you’re relying on their bassinets. Other airlines, like Singapore Airlines and Virgin Australia, provide larger bassinets that go up to 16–18 kg, and their crews are far more accommodating to families. Verdict: Misleading information, zero empathy, and unhelpful staff. Not a family-friendly airline.

author: Ken Howie
review_text: Not Verified | Business class flight from Durban to London via Dubai. Used the chauffeur service which was excellent. Check in and formalities were very quick, and I was in the lounge within 15 minutes of arrival. The 777 shows signs of its age, especially with the 232 seating, but this was not a problem, as with only 4 passengers in the forward cabin everybody had a double seat. The seats are angle flat, which was not really an issue. I was quickly offered a glass of champagne, the start of excellent service throughout the flight. Drinks and snacks were served after take off, with the meal following a hour later. I opted for soup, which was superb, followed by lamb wellington which was disappointing, finishing with a nice selection of cheese with a glass of port. The selection of wines was good. It was noticeable how noisy the 777 was, compared with more modern aircraft. The seat despite not being fully flat was comfortable, permitting a few hours sleep before arrival in Dubai. Any shortcomings in the aircraft were made up for by the superb service throughout the flight. The second leg was on the A380, which lived up to the promises of the adverts. Lots of space, lots of storage, and a fully lie flat bed with good leg/foot space. The high standard of service continued.. I slept for a few hours after take off, giving breakfast a miss. The onboard bar seemed popular, and whilst not using it, passed through on the way to the toilets, which are right at the back beyond the bar. These are the only toilets, which are some distance if sitting at the front of the cabin. Service is from a galley beyond the bar, so there is a fair amount of traffic up the aisle. Lunch was served about 2 hour’s before landing. Again a superb soup starter, disappointing main course, and excellent wines. In London I used the chauffeur service, which was excellent. All in all this was an excellent trip, marked by superb service.

author: S Gan
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   My Samsonite was damage on the flight Melbourne to London 26 June. The damage was reported the next day. Dina from Emirates Customer Care wrote back to say it must be reported at the airport although the law allows 7 days for filing a report. I emailed photos of the damage and also advised that I was leaving UK on the 4 Jul. Dina emailed on the 4 Jul that the suitcase would be collected to be repaired. I had left the suitcase with my mother in the UK. Failed collection over 3 days as Emirates had given the incorrect address. 28 Jul Emirates emailed to say Samsonite has been repaired and will be dropped off where it was collected in UK. Bear in mind, I had been emailing constantly to chase up and to find out what was going. The Montreal Convention - which Emirates is part of - states that the repaired suitcase has to be delivered to the passenger. Emirates refuses to do so. Very disappointing service - Emirates dragged their feet responding to emails and when finally had to act, took so long that by the time they fixed the suitcase I was back in Australia. Emirates refuses to send the repaired suitcase back. Utterly disgraceful behaviour.

author: Stephen Hesketh
review_text: Not Verified |   Seat 57g aisle seat must have been one of the most threadbare and uncomfortable seats I have ever had the misfortune to be seated on (an A380-800, a very old one). Food was way below par from what it once was. Boeing 777 was a very old one, also noisy and not been updated, not comfortable.

author: Liz Wahlen
review_text: Not Verified |   I flew on Emirates for the first time last month and was extremely disappointed. They did not follow through with their promised services, so don't be fooled. They offer a fancy, glossy package of business class, but the reality is they don't meet what's advertised. My flight was delayed landing in Dubai, but rather than drive me to my next flight as promised, they decided I wouldn't be able to make it and cancelled my ticket before I even tried. I asked the drivers at the gate if they would kindly take me, and I was denied. I ran 20 minutes across the airport, and arrived on time but was told they had made the decision for me. My baggage was delayed by 2.5 days - they couldn't explain why it wasn't loaded on the next two flights. My meal was also no longer available since they had taken me off the flight. I was also promised reimbursement of expenses upon arrival. I had a large presentation the following day, and none of my expenses for that meeting were covered. I also had a very rude driver getting to the airport. Don't trust the airline, and definitely don't trust their layovers. It's really too bad - I was looking for a new primary airline for business travel, and it certainly won't be Emirates.

author: Jeena Thomas
review_text: Not Verified |    I was on flight EK344 from Dubai to Malaysia on [07/07/2025]. Despite the 7-hour flight duration, the second meal service was skipped entirely. No announcement or explanation was provided by the crew. I would appreciate an explanation and appropriate compensation.

author: Axel Lorsold
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | I contacted Emirate to make sure my 74 year old mom who has difficulties to walk would get wheel chair assistance. The service was not provided in Dubai, both ways. I sent a complaint and the staff had the audacity to answer me that they checked with the staff and that my mom received assistance. Basically calling her a liar. She wrote back, stating the detail of her experience. I additionally required to check the CCTV to confirm what my mom experienced. The response I received was that they would basically only take in consideration the staff version of the story and give 15000 complimentary skywards miles as a “gesture of goodwill”. Emirates never acknowledged their mistake. And they have the audacity to give my mother miles, in case she wants to experience their pathetic service again. The audacity has no limit.

author: Darrell Parsons
review_text: Not Verified |  Travelled with Emirates in April 2024. Baggage was lost / delayed for 5 days on arrival at MUC. Submitted claim for emergency essentials totalling €716.13, all receipts provided. Emirates agreed to pay €219 which I rejected and after numerous ongoing emails to them, no communication at all apart from from an auto reply stating it’s on review and I will be contacted in 14 days, over a year now and nothing and I will continue to take this further until full reimbursement of a legitimate claim is settled. Disgraceful service from Emirates, of which I was once a Gold member. Would not recommend Emirates Airlines to anyone anymore, worst service ever experienced!

author: H Varish
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   My father expired on Jun 17th 2025 and I had to attend funeral, this is emergency travel on June 18th 2025. I had almost no time to convince my manager at work and get emergency passport renewal. When I checked their fares, they were very high. Normally it should be around 1300 CAD in their Economy class one way but it shows 2400 CAD ( 4 seats left ) while checking their fares on their web site. While booking I got a call from my boss, after 10 minutes it shows the fare increased to 2700 CAD and shows only 2 seats left. I was worried and booked it. I cannot select seat due to last minute booking. When I reached airport the check in lady said only aisle seats available but the 3 seats next to me will be empty, if they assign someone there ask them to give you another seat. Not sure what this makes. I cannot sleep on those empty seats, just can stretch my legs. They did not assign anyone in those seats but Emirates air hostess and staff on flight keep looking at me strangely. When I checked the other seats I see other passengers have empty seats in Economy class next to my row and they were sleeping on them. I paid double the normal fare and it is not a last minute pleasure trip. I see more than 30 empty seats on the flight within the 4 rows front and behind my row in economy class. I was not assigned a seat in Dubai to Hyderabad flight but issued boarding pass in Toronto. Eventually they gave me Business class aisle seat, that flight is only 3.5 hours and I could not sleep in that short period. The food and drinks they offered in business class is same as in economy class. Their food is Indian cuisine which was ok to me. Shame on Emirates with this type of wrong news about availability of seats and impersistent seat allocation. Decided never travel on Emirates flights in future. Advise other travelers never fly on Emirates. Though food was good but all the free beers, vodka, or scotch whiskey is not worth the price you pay. Very bad experience.

author: Maryam Sadeghi
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Emirates is the worst experience I have ever had.  Bad food, rude staff, awful airport and the worst service. They did not dispatch my luggage. I am waiting for it for days. Every day, they were calling me that your luggage will be delivered today and I had to stay at home. But they did not. The airport was the worst. Tap water was warm. There was not enough seats for people in front of gates. While Qatar Airways airport in Doha has separate spacious room with comfortable seats for ladies, there was not such a thing in Emirates airport. You had to pay for every single basic single. I never will fly with Emirates again.

author: Mark Zambelli
review_text: Not Verified |  Very comfortable flight and good service. Seat was comfortable. Entertainment system wasn’t that great and not many good movies. The food was disappointing bland and lacking flavour.

author: Christian Prade
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Economy class, Zurich to Dubai was a nightmare! Delayed departure, 380 people standing (very few seats occupied), crowded in a hot room with no air or window. The A380 was old and not upgraded. The TV screen broke after 30 minutes flight. My wife called 2 times. 2 different annoyed crew responded "I'll come back to fix it". They never come back and no ICE system available during the entire flight. Worse, I ordered a $600 watch. The steward told me "I ll bring to you" 4 hours later, just before landing, he was taking pictures of passenger. I told him "What about my watch" He mumbled "sorry I have forgotten". I complained to his chief and of course cancelled my order. Return in their new Premium Economy class. Again a nightmare with no dedicated check in counter contrary to what they advertise, I have to wait 20 minutes. The flight was OK but at the level of other premium economy class. Emirates is expensive compared to other airlines but the huge price difference was once warranted by clean new aircrafts, Top entertainment, caring to passengers, and good service - but no more! I really prefer Etihad that flight out of nearby new Abu Dhabi airport. In comparison Dubai DXB looks now old.

author: Muhamad Mostafa
review_text: Not Verified |  The cabin service was horrible. Imagine seating aisle side and the push cart being ramp straight to your knee.  No apologies what so ever.  Similar things seem to happen to other passengers but the crew didn't seem to care that much. Aside from that, they just chug the food tray to you without even asking what meal you would like. I don't know what's their deal or if the  crew is having a bad moody day. But may I suggest not taking it out on the passengers who have earnestly paid for their flight.

author: Loay Osman
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   First leg DXB-BKK was on the A380 the crew were very nice and welcoming. I managed to sleep the entire flight with comfy bedding and lovely amenities kit. The return flight CGK-DXB was a lovely flight with amazing crew who came to check on me several times specially the business class supervisor who was from Uzbekistan. The meal service was also great and managed to sleep for few hours. After landing we were escorted to our bus to arrivals and in few minutes was out and my luggage were waiting for me et the belt and the chauffeur service was also excellent.

author: Wayne Good
review_text: Not Verified | Amsterdam to Dubai in economy. Premium Economy not available on this sector. Paid extra for bulk head seat. Good flight, meal, service etc. Due to Emirates status, used lounge in Amsterdam. It’s a contract lounge and is awful. Over crowded and just unpleasant. Total contrast in Dubai. Terminal A lounge is vast and very well appointed. Dubai to Auckland departing 13th June in Premium Economy. Seat 34J. I’m writing this because I had the best flight attendant and service I have ever had with Emirates including my experiences in Business. She went over and beyond and was totally charming. I wish I could remember her name, she was from Argentina. I actually spoke to the Cabin Manager about her. An absolute star. Again good food and I do find the seat very comfortable. Always manage a good sleep. I like Emirates and they are my long haul airline of choice.

author: Brian Ohame
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   What a horrible flight experience on Flight EK730, B777-300 on 28.05.2025. hecked in well, and then proceeded to board B777 - 300 where I found a Tired, Stressed or rather irritated crew member - my partner and i were seated on 47A/47B which she was shocked with that came with a loud question "are you staff?" My partner looking at me in wonder and bothered. We responded No we are not. She then demanded our boarding pass which indicated our seat numbers. She still looked puzzled like we were seated in a wrong place or on a wrong flight as she returned the passes to us. All our smiles and warmth were shuttered by this staff hardly taking off. We then got worried of if she will be the one attending to us and it turned out we were right to worry. As if that wasn't enough, time for our long waited meal came and  the crew to serve was the same. She tells us she only has Chicken for main  like there was no Menu that was issued prior to our meal - my partner doesn't eat chicken, mushrooms but not allergic and I don't fancy them either. We politely told her we want 2 beef. And she was like only chicken available. I repeated we want 2 beef as we don't eat chicken. Said since you don't want to eat chicken I can only give you the plate with a starter and Desert without the main. As I got shocked with how much I paid for our ticket with no discount or promotion. But we are being served like we are being done a favour. A huge thanks to her colleague who was so lively, sweet and professional. I guess she noticed how un happy we were.

author: Wayne Good
review_text: Not Verified |  Auckland to Dubai Premium Economy. Comfortable seat with good recline. Slept a good solid 7 hours. Food good, service not so good. Definitely had better crews in the past. Service was slow, dinner trays left for a long time. Had to alert a cabin attendant to take mine away. Dubai to Paris economy. Seat ok, service quite good and very good food. There is no other airline for me.

author: Graham Henrickson
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   I guess I didn’t fit the mould of a typical Emirates first class passenger, because despite presenting my boarding pass, I was directed to the first seat on my right and found myself in business class at seat 7A. There were a few red faces when I came back and said that’s not the seat on my boarding pass – 1A. I was whisked away by the Purser amid a hail of apologies and the promise they would make up for it, and they certainly did. When it comes to typical flight times for an Airbus A380, at around 3 hours, the trip from Christchurch to Sydney is just a blip. Thanks to the great crew, I had the opportunity to enjoy the full first class experience. Dom Perignon was being poured within minutes of entering my suite and I was presented with the first-class menu. Before take-off I was given a set of PJ’s and fabric carry bag to take them home in. Then as the aircraft levelled out the meal service started with an enormous serving of caviar with the offer of more, followed by a melody of dishes that were to die for. After dinner, I accepted the bed turndown service. In addition to the luxurious padded seat, they attach a mattress along with a white sheet and a big fluffy pillow. Without ear plugs or a sleeping mask, I was asleep in less than 10 minutes and slept soundly for over an hour surrounded by the twinkling lights installed in the ceiling overhead as well as the floor. Tempted as I was to accept the invitation to try out the onboard shower, I felt that might be just a little too decadent for a 3-hour flight.  When I returned after changing from PJ’s back to my travel clothes the bed had returned to being a seat and my jacket and shoes were neatly arranged. We landed into Sydney 20min ahead of schedule and on a Friday night.

author: G Miller
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | I had the worst experience at Miami on April 12, 2025. My trip was MIA-BOG. The people at the counter were very rude. I always use a small luggage as a personal item (under seat cabin bag), accepted at ALL airlines, but Emirates didn't accept it. When I told the counter agent that this baggage is accepted on all airlines as a personal item, he rudely told me that those were Emirates's rules and that in "someone else's home, the rules must be obey.” He also criticized me for traveling in economy class. Also, when I tried to buy in the app the extra baggage, I choose the extra baggage for the route MIA-BOG, but when I clicked "continue" the site changed the route to BOG-MIA. I noted the mistake when I receive the confirmation by email. Inmediatelly I called Emirates Customer Service but they refused to made me a refund. Now, I had to pay $100 at the counter and I lost the $130 that I paid in the app, because I don't need any extra bagagge for the route BOG-MIA. In addition to the unexpected expense, this experience ruined my trip.

author: Franck Janet
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   In my opinion, Emirates is highly overrated. It is often promoted as a top-tier airline, but my experience tells a different story. In economy class, the service is underwhelming at best. On this flight to Paris, I was nearly bumped to a later flight due to overbooking, and I had to insist firmly in order to be accommodated. The in-flight experience left much to be desired. The food was disappointing, the service was average, and the cabin felt overcrowded. I requested a glass of water which never arrived. I pressed the call button, but no one responded. Between Dubai and Paris, not once did the crew proactively offer water. As for business class – although I wasn’t flying in that cabin on this occasion, I have done so in the past – Emirates often charges a premium that is difficult to justify given the level of service compared to competitors. I also purchased a Wi-Fi session, which was advertised as high-speed internet. In reality, the download speed was just 2.82 Mbps and the upload speed only 1.78 Mbps – simply unacceptable. To add to the poor impression, the crew announced the wrong time upon arrival in Paris, a basic error that speaks to a lack of attention to detail. The cabin crew, for the most part, were unsmiling and disengaged. Overall, Emirates is no longer the exceptional airline it once was. In economy class, it feels more like a cattle car in the sky than a premium travel experience.

author: S Peale
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Having paid to choose our seats on this flight there was an aircraft change and we did not get the seats that we paid for. Despite several email and telephone calls Emirates have refused to refund what is a relatively small amount of money quoting ‘terms and conditions’, although their terms and conditions state that we are entitled to a refund. They used to be a good airline and we have flown with them fairly often. However we will not be using them again.

author: Berton
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   An uneventful flight to Amsterdam. Catering was not the best this time: bland food and sides. We were served twice, it filled our stomach but that was it. Service provided by the staff was friendly and speedy despite a full plane. Seats were comfortable. We landed 30 min earlier in Amsterdam.

author: B Koslov
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | The most unprofessional staff I’ve ever seen. Had to use Emirates as backup because Cathay Pacific delayed our flight. Maybe because of that seat selection was not available for us. That one I do not blame this airline on. But: We got two seats way back at the end of 777. Behind me was a man in his 50s. At the altitude I reclined my seat (not all the way back) and was prepared to get some sleep in this 6 hr flight. Immidiately I feel tap on my shoulder and some arguing that I have to raise my seat. He was arguing that he could not eat with my seat reclined. I tried to explain that my seat does not affect his table position, but really I feel like he just wanted more space. He was really unpleasant to talk to, it felt like there was only his needs and everyone around should just obey to that. English is not my native languge, so I finished the argument with "ask the flight attendant", I was sure that she can explain everything better than me. The man catches flight attendant, explains that he want me to raise my seat. She does not ask any questions, just stands up near me and commands "raise your seat" and proceeds with taking back of my seat and tries to raise it with force. No questions asked. With flight attendant fully on his side I even did not even try to argue. It felt really dengerous to even talk back to these people. Food was given 2 hours (!) after take off. After food serving nobody did not even try to provide us with any sort of bevereges. Again, that is on 6 hrs flight. Is that even legal? We had to catch flight attendant to ask for any water-like substance. How dare you to ask me about upgrades to premium economy or business if you fail to provide any basic service for economy? Or does Emirates starts to provide basic service starting from business? It is logical to just use better airlines instead. It is a level lower than any low-cost airline in the Eastern Europe. I am a frequent flyer and did not expect something like that at the price that I paid. It is by far my worst flight expirience. My family and friends will never use Emirates ever again.

author: Yu-Hsiu Chang
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   The cabin is clean. Flight attendants are friendly and polite. Seats are comfortable and can be reclined easily. The food is delicious. Flights departed on time.

author: N Sabetian
review_text: Not Verified |  I will never fly with them again, they have poor customer care. Long-story short, our flight was cancelled after waiting on the plane for several hours, at 2 AM and under the rain, with two young children we had to find a hotel, catch a taxi and recheck everything out of the airport and then back in. Our luggage had been mishandled and all clothes wet. They wouldnt reimburse for costs incurred as they are counting dollars and cents at present. I wouldnt touch them again, they charge a very large sum of money and their after sale services are very poor

author: Yvonne Weston
review_text: Not Verified |  I dashed across Dubai airport, having an hour and a half transit time since my connecting flight from Bangkok. There was no time to get a drink. I was relieved to get my flight to Birmingham. I was hot and thirsty. Unfortunately, for a torturous 2 hours and 50 minutes, there wasn't a drop of liquid served, although I did ask for a glass of water, which never transpired. Apart from that, which, when you're tired and thirsty, seems a massive problem.

author: George Stainton
review_text: Not Verified |  Emirates lost my luggage 9 months ago and have still not dealt with the complaint. No PIR number was provided as the team at Manchester airport were very unorganised. All they asked me to do was fill out an online form, through GBS Enquiries which I did. I have been back and fourth and had multiple phone calls with the team but the complaint still has not been dealt with. The customer service has been extremely poor. I'm very disappointed with Emirates.

author: Denis Mbanga
review_text: Not Verified | Emirates delayed flight from Washington D.C to Dubai, then me and my group missed our flight to Dar. Emirates gave us a hotel booking and an alternative flight for the next day. But it is so weired we have never get any support into getting to the hotel. Its so sad that Emirates has started being a Zero Star Airline.
route: Washington D.C to Dar es Salaam via Dubai

author: E Baile
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   We were excited to fly with this airline for the first time. There were four of us (my husband, my two kids, and myself). We used points for three tickets and paid in full cash for the four ticket. We have business class one way. Not only was the cabin crew horrible from Miami to Dubai (they disappeared shortly into the flight and didn't resurface till the end of the flight. They left a table of snacks and wine and water by the bathroom), but they badly damaged my bag. My bag was just two weeks old and has tears and rips in it. The only way to file a complaint or notify them of your damage bag is to fill out an online complete form. It's the worst way of communication. They take weeks to get back to you and then will give you different excuses every time. They are the most unprofessional Employees I have ever worked with in my life. I feel like I was cheated and robbed from them. We spent over 450,000 points, and 7000 in cash in fees for one way tickets all to have horrible customer service, a damaged bag, and bad flight crew. Avoid this airline like the plague.

author: Shadi Alkasim
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Boarding an A380 was a unique experience and you will enjoy a pleasant flight thanks to the spaciousness and comfort. The cabin crew were admirable and friendly, the food was good and delicious. Highly recommended!

author: C Hewett
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Bitterly disappointed in Emirates. I was promised that I will get A Dubai Connect option in Dubai with my flight only to be told that I won’t. I have a layover of 20 hours and my husband is on the same journey with the shorter layover yet he received Dubai Connect. Never traveling with Emirates again.
route: Cape Town to Sydney via Dubai

author: Franck Janet
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | The flight was scheduled for 9:30 AM but was delayed by more than 5 hours. Nearly every hour, we received announcements that the flight was being delayed by yet another hour or two. Such a delay, coupled with the treatment of passengers, is unacceptable. I am deeply disappointed with Emirates.

author: Stuart Ballantyne
review_text: Not Verified | Flights from Australia to Europe return went mostly OK. The larger issue I had was with FF miles. It was not allocated to my account when flights were booked. Eventually I found this out. Due to an ongoing software issue with Emirates website I was unable to log into my account. After multiple calls and emails they said they were "working on it". I was finally able to log in after 6 months, now points have expired. Emirates refused to credit these due to policy. Booking several flights (work and personal) shortly to Europe and USA but not with Emirates.

author: Graeme Lowther
review_text: Not Verified | Wow! Ever since the the Aussie exec management left the airline, Emirates had been in a quality nose dive. It has gone from being a luxury carrier to being more like a low cost airline. Flying in business class now feels like economy used to be. Here is how the quality has collapsed IMO You no longer get an amenities bag unless you are overnight.
