My screen had issues which was frustrating though. Staff very friendlya and approachable. Food very good! Second leg not as good. Same plane but older layout. Food not as good. Really horrible sandwich, and my breakfast was only OK, not that appetising. Seat also not very comfortable (35C exit seat). I always have to pay for exit seats because of my height. I get annoyed when people see empty ones and sit in them when they haven't paid. There were quite a few empty seats on both legs of the journey, yet when I booked 48hrs before departure, there was only 1 seat left. Toilets kept quite clean, but the bins were overflowing on both flights.  Both flights delayed without explanation. Flight arrived 10mins early at final destination. Doha airport I find good. My second flight was not shown on the screens though, so there were a lot of people trying to flag down staff to check what gate.

author: J Hayne
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Evening departure from BKK. Qatar really struggle with boarding on occasions and this was no different. Seats were changed at the gate as one of our reserved one’s were wet. Allocated into the rear cabin 38A + B. Seemed to be an older aircraft with an older configuration in the business cabin. Busy flight. The seat proved to be very comfortable and superbly thought out. The best there is I think. Safety issue of individuals roaming around the cabin aisles looking for empty seat rows, including someone moving up and down the aisle with his bags, opening and shutting overhead bins blocking the aisle While the aircraft is taxiing under power for departure. Something that should of been jumped on very quickly, but wasn’t. Food was exceptional for Economy, as was the service from a hard working pleasant crew. Overall this sector proved that this is the best Medium to long haul Economy cabin product there is. . Doha Hamad Airport is exceptional and a pleasant transfer. Second Sector on a Boeing 787-8. 19F + G either side of an aisle. Flight appeared to be full and Departed on time, early hours of the morning. The seat’s on this Aircraft were significantly less comfortable. A . 3-3-3 configuration and the ACDFGJ seats each have an under seat IFE box mounted on it’s side that restricts the width of legroom available. Seats appear far narrower, and not so well thought out. Although I find the cabin appealing and the ride pleasant. I’ll generally avoid this particular type of Aircraft. because I find them particularly uncomfortable in Economy, especially on a busy flight.. Again, exceptional food, great Service and a lovely hard working crew. Nonetheless, overall a very nice Economy experience, highly recommend it.

author: Rashid Alammari
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   As a frequent flyer with Qatar Airways, I can confidently say that their service is consistently exceptional. The hospitality, from check-in to arrival, is outstanding; staff are courteous, attentive, and always ready to assist. Their scheduling is reliable and well-organized, making flights punctual and connections smooth. The ease of booking, online or through the app is incredibly user-friendly, allowing me to arrange trips without hassle. The lounge facilities are superb, offering a quiet, luxurious space to relax before flights with excellent dining options. Both ground and inflight services are top-notch, with a focus on comfort, quality, and efficiency. Qatar Airways truly sets a high standard in global air travel!

author: A Mears
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Doha to Athens plane was small with box that blocked leg room window seats. As a person with a disability I could not move, request to move was met with only had middle seat, as business class is only for people that pay for them. When I requested to pay by points for upgrade was told none available. When people in front chose to recline hostess reaction they are allowed to recline however when we tried our seats were rudely pushed upright by passengers. I have emailed Qatar as yet no response.

author: Martin Halshaw
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   In the past 10 days or so I've taken 4 long haul business class flights with Qatar and on all of them it's been like being in a 5 star hotel / restaurant. The cabin crew treated me like a VIP, the food & drinks were excellent and the facilities (seat, entertainment, wifi, toilets etc) were all fantastic. It is a real pleasure flying QA. The same goes for the lounges I used in Doha with the only negative being the lounges which they don't control outside of Doha.

author: Brian Davies
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Absolutely terrible trip. Started off well from Dubai to Doha nice 777 in first class which is business class rebranded for this route. Once in Doha the fun started in the Business Class lounge I was told I could only stay 30 minutes and access to the restaurant area was denied because they were busy, so no hot food. Staff were robotic and not at all interested. The connecting flight was an old A320 with a business class seat which was broken and they said cannot be fixed. Hardly any legroom and cramped. Poor inflight entertainment selection and no wifi. Breakfast portions dismal, left the flight hungry.

author: R Han
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   I discovered that my luggage had been severely damaged during the journey. The crack spanned across the depth of the luggage, from the zipper to the wheel area, and the inner linings of my baggage were clearly visible. As I had left the Airport premises when the damage was found and I acknowledged that there might not be anything the airline could have done for me, their response was the most unhelpful I have ever received. My return flight on 29 September was cancelled. The instructions to collect our baggage and hotel vouchers were poorly communicated, we only heard muffled announcements and did not receive any email or text message on what to do next. It was chaotic and the airline staff were unhelpful, it took us more than 4 hours just to collect our baggage and vouchers at the airport, before we boarded the bus to the assigned hotel.  Following my trip, I also reached out to Qatar Airways Media/Customer Service to share my feedback, however, it does not seem like they took my feedback seriously. They took more than 10 days to inform me that they had forwarded my feedback on baggage irregularities to the Baggage department in Zurich.

author: C Mitchell
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | The experience from boarding, which was chaotic and confusing, to the seat, entertainment, staff and food was abysmal. Qatar have really gone downhill. During boarding the staff were giving contradictory messages to the passengers, with one person saying a certain group could board and another saying they couldn't. The economy seats are hard, small and uncomfortable. I was able to book an economy comfort++ for one leg of my journey. It should have been two but they changed the hardware, so I was bumped to economy. These seats are much better but it's a lottery if you can book one. My food servings were tiny, and a couple of the meals I couldn't finish they were that bad. The staff were didn't do anything above the bare minimum. The entertainment system on some planes is outdated and unresponsive, although much better on the newer planes. However, the selection of films is quite poor.

author: Craig Cutts
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   I have flown with QR 8 times this month, economy and business class. The airline is pretty good especially in economy as a Privilege club member with status, expedited check in and lounge access for both Silver & Gold levels. On board assuming you pick the right seat it's comfortable The food is good as is the service, it's very good and probably one of the best. Business class is great on any aircraft, I had my first experience of Q Suites which was nice, although I like the A380 too with a bit more space and a lounge to use. My 8th flight this month in Q suites from DOH to LHR was probably the least enjoyable, boarding was a shambles, the aircraft was a 20 minute bus ride away and once on board remained at 30c + for 45 minutes, the crew were just okay. Food options not available and the area around my seat is not cleaned with rubbish left by the previous passenger. Clearly QR and DOH airport offer great options, we all have off days so hopefully this is what happened with my last flight. Otherwise I will continue to use QR on my 8 to 10 trips each year, they really are customer focused and offer a great product they just need to get there boarding process sorted it's a bit of a let down sometimes.

author: K Hang
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | My experience on EY498, AUH–SIN, on 27 June, in The Residence, was one of the worst flight experiences I have had. The Residence should be Etihad’s halo product, but this journey felt fragmented from beginning to end. At Emirates Palace, I had Home Check-in scheduled between 14:00 and 15:00, with chauffeur pick-up at 15:00. The chauffeur arrived at 14:45, while the Morafiq Home Check-in staff appeared only at 14:55. The chauffeur did not seem to understand Home Check-in and questioned why I was checking in at the hotel rather than at the airport. I had to contact The Residence Concierge several times during hotel check-out. At one point, I wanted to cancel Home Check-in and proceed to airport check-in, but there was no clear way to communicate that request. The experience was chaotic, and no one apologized or took ownership. At AUH Terminal A, despite arriving in an airline-arranged chauffeur vehicle, there was no seamless curbside handover to Etihad ground staff. We were simply dropped off and had to find our own way to the First Class check-in area. Onboard, the product was not the main issue. The problem was service attitude. The crew member in charge of The Residence cabin was curt and not particularly welcoming. When we wanted to use the shower facility, it felt as though this was being treated as an inconvenience. We felt hurried while using a facility that should be central to the premium experience. I only learned just before disembarking that there had been a Korean-speaking crew member onboard. She spoke to us in Korean as we were leaving and said she had wanted to greet us earlier but had been too busy. Finding this out only at the very end was disappointing. The crème de la crème was the Meet & Greet service at Singapore Changi Airport. A staff member was waiting with my name on a sign, but she was alone and was also responsible for other passengers. For the first time in my experience, I had a Meet & Greet staff member present but still had to carry multiple pieces of luggage myself. Changi is highly automated and immigration is usually fast, so the practical value of Meet & Greet there is mostly assistance and luggage handling. The cabin crew had not reminded us about Singapore’s arrival QR procedure, so we had to complete it hurriedly in front of immigration. At that moment, the Meet & Greet staff member said she had to step away to assist other customers. I felt less like a premium passenger and more like a child being shepherded by a kindergarten teacher. If one staff member must look after multiple passengers, surely passengers arriving from The Residence should be the highest priority. While we were waiting for the chauffeur, she disappeared without even saying goodbye. In its own way, it was the perfect ending to the whole production. I did not complain during the journey. I even tipped the unfriendly chauffeur. I usually do not write harsh reviews; I simply choose not to use the service again. The Residence is still Etihad’s halo product and should be built on a true First Class service premise. Yet the best thing about The Residence was the Voss sparkling water in the glass bottle inside the fridge. I did not drink it.

author: E Hadani
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | In the past few years, we see a complete mismanagement of this airline. I never had this kind of the problem with Etihad Airways before but lately, I often see a change in my travel dates even though the original flight I booked was not cancelled. I normally make my flight booking months in advance, but I often receive an email that says my flight is moved to another day.  I can no longer depend on this airline. During April 2026, my weekend flight was moved twice, and my final flight was put during the weekdays and that caused me a lot of grief with my current employer. My employer thought I was trying to have longer vacation, which was not true. The number of complaints is growing but management seems to ignore these complaints. I am again travelling overseas from Abu Dhabi in July 2026, and my tickets were purchased in early May, two months ago, but I received an email, just today, and I am told that my flight is delayed by two days. As a 4-Star Airline, Hadani Etihad can no longer be trusted. I see no point of planning ahead since Etihad airways can just change flight dates whenever it feels like it. Terrible.

author: Florian Gerth
review_text: Not Verified | Absolutely terrible experience. The most unreliable airline in the world. They keep on changing their schedule and make the result your, and only your problem. Each and every person working in their customer service gives you a different opinion. None of which is of any help and none of which is correct. This is absolutey disgusting. A complete insult given the money you pay. Terrible!
route: Manila to Frankfurt via Abu Dhabi

author: Stamatios Morakis
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | It started with a minor 1-hour and 14-minute delay on my initial flight from Tokyo (NRT). Before takeoff, I asked Etihad staff if I would miss my connection. They said "No need to worry, the system knows, they are prepared, and you have plenty of time." The delay didn't change, yet upon landing in Abu Dhabi (AUH), instead of rushing connecting passengers to the departing gates, Etihad staff intercepted and blocked us from reaching the Athens gate, forcing us to miss the flight. After hours of waiting in lines, Etihad first tried to makr me to wait 1.5 days for their next flight. When I refused, they rerouted me through Cairo via EgyptAir, claiming no other options existed—despite online availability on much better airlines. This resulted in a 12-hour arrival delay in Athens, a missed working day, and a sleepless night.  Instead of providing hotel accommodation or lounge access, Etihad staff forced me into a customer holding area called the "Guest Service Centre." The conditions were shocking: the room was filthy, filled with garbage, emitted a foul odor. My luggage was lost during this rerouting and took 3 days to be recovered, having to return to the airport myself to claim it. When I contacted Etihad Guest Relations, they sent a robotic response dodging all liability, blaming air traffic, and washing their hands by telling me to contact EgyptAir. Etihad’s premium image is a complete, fraudulent illusion. The moment something goes wrong, they treat paying passengers with absolute contempt and zero respect.
route: Narita to Athens via Abu Dhabi

author: Anna Bauerová
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   On May 4, 2026, during my connection in Abu Dhabi, something apparently happened at the airport and several departing flights were suddenly subjected to an additional security screening at a single gate. The issue was not the extra screening itself, but the complete lack of organization and communication. Passengers travelling to Egypt, Manchester, Jordan, Germany, and other destinations were all directed into one overcrowded gate area. Nobody explained what was happening. Staff appeared overwhelmed, communication was poor, and the entire process felt disorganized. We spent around an hour standing in a packed crowd with little room to move, no available seating, and very limited information. The situation became increasingly uncomfortable as the gate area grew more crowded. Despite the conditions, no refreshments were provided. The situation worsened after boarding, when the aircraft remained on the runway for approximately four additional hours. I understand that delays can occur, but I was disappointed by the limited communication and customer care during this period. At one point, the cabin crew distributed some water, but only limited refreshments were provided despite the lengthy delay. There was also no complimentary Wi-Fi available, making it difficult for passengers to update family members, rearrange plans, or deal with missed connections. As a result of the delay, I missed my onward transportation from Munich despite allowing what should have been a generous connection buffer. During other flights on the same trip, I also observed situations that reflected poorly on customer service. For example, a passenger who had paid extra for a seat with additional legroom was moved following an aircraft change and appeared to receive little explanation or apology. In several interactions, staff came across as dismissive and unhelpful. Etihad markets itself as a premium airline and charges prices that reflect that positioning. Based on my experience, the service, communication, and handling of disruptions fell well below those expectations. I did not expect perfection, but I did expect clear communication, respect for passengers, and reasonable care during a major delay. Based on this experience, I do not intend to fly with Etihad again and would not recommend the airline. The quality of the onboard food was also disappointing, and the portions felt inadequate, particularly given that the flight lasted several hours longer than scheduled.
route: Hanoi to Munich via Abu Dhabi

author: Yi Huei Lu
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Terrible customer experience. Etihad Airways closed their local representative office in Taiwan and disabled their local toll-free line, leaving local passengers completely abandoned with zero communication channels. We are facing severe geopolitical conflict risks in the Middle East for our upcoming flights in late August, yet Etihad imposes discriminatory waiver policies. New bookings enjoy free changes, while loyal customers who booked earlier are forced to pay hefty change fees for facing the exact same war-zone risks. Frontline support only provides robotic, unhelpful automated templates.
route: Taipei to Milan via Abu Dabi

author: Isabel Sanchez Alonso
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |  We were denied boarding in February 2026 due to overbooking on flight EY101 from Abu Dhabi to Madrid despite having confirmed tickets. This flight was part of our return journey from the Maldives (Madrid–Malé–Madrid), which made the disruption even more significant after a long international trip. At Abu Dhabi Airport, airline staff informed us that compensation related to the denied boarding would be processed after we submitted a claim. Based on this information, we expected compensation reflecting the serious disruption caused by the overbooking and the fact that we arrived in Madrid more than 11 hours later than scheduled. However, after completing the claims process, the only compensation offered was a USD 200 voucher. This outcome was very different from the expectations created by the information provided at the airport. I cannot help feeling that we were misled regarding the compensation that would follow. Had we known that the final outcome would be a USD 200 voucher for three passengers after an 11-hour delay caused by overbooking, our expectations would have been very different. I am sharing this experience so that other passengers are aware of what happened and can make informed decisions if they find themselves in a similar situation.
route: Male to Madrid via Abu Dhabi

author: S Valenci
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Etihad is a perfect example of a company that charges premium prices while delivering a substandard customer experience. Their customer service is among the worst I have ever dealt with. Before the flight, during the journey, and after the trip, every interaction felt like a battle. Nobody seems empowered to solve problems, communication is poor, and their internal processes are painfully inefficient. Etihad charges premium prices, but delivers a disappointing customer experience and does not issue refunds after a flight cancellation. The customer service is extremely difficult to reach and largely ineffective. Before, during, and after my trip, getting assistance felt impossible. Communication was poor, issues were not properly handled, and I was repeatedly passed between departments without receiving clear answers. What frustrated me most was the lack of transparency regarding procedures and requirements when support was needed. Instead of helping passengers, the process seemed designed to make resolving problems as difficult as possible. The onboard experience was average and certainly not worth the high fares. Overall, one of the most disappointing airline experiences I have had. I would not fly with Etihad again and would not recommend it.
route: Rome to Hong Kong via Abu Dhabi

author: Ana Silva
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Etihad cancelled our booking and failed to provide adequate support. After the cancellation, we repeatedly attempted to contact Etihad by phone in order to receive alternative flight options and assistance. Despite several attempts, we were left waiting every time, (once for more than 5 hours) without any support or viable travel alternatives being provided. The options offered were non-sense (as in not the same route we needed!). Therefore we were forced to purchase new tickets with another airline at our own expense. We submitted formal complaints and follow-up emails on 7 March, 8 March, 30 March, and 13 April, explaining the situation and requesting reimbursement of the alternative flights. Despite this, Etihad so far never formally replied to any of our communications. The airline later processed only a partial refund related to the unused flight segment, while ignoring the additional costs we incurred due to their failure to assist passengers. Etihad is not complying with EU law and this experience showed an unacceptable lack of customer support, communication, and responsibility toward passengers affected by cancellations.
route: Narita to Lisbon via Abu Dhabi

author: Chris Sansom
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |  On the first leg CMB-AUH A320 had the exit row 3 seats to myself so comfortable, inflight catering of a high standard and cabin crew very good. The second flight on an A350-1000 that was relatively new had large entertainment screens and a good choice to view and listen to. A special mention goes who were very caring, professional and sociable. The Chicken Birryani and the pizza prior to landing very tasty. The crew offered drinks throughout the flight and the bar was open for top ups. Staff kept the washrooms refreshed throughout the flight. Very enjoyable flights.
route: Colombo to London Heathrow via Abu Dhabi

author: Chris Sansom
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Great flight with 3 seats to myself. The cabin crew were excellent, it was my Birthday during my week away I was served with a card, cake and drink. The catering and bar service led to a very comfortable journey and the large entertainment screens was easy to operate. The second flight on the A320 EY392 also very good.
route: London to Colombo via Abu Dhabi

author: S Darkevi
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Very disappointed with the attitude of crew in general. After take off seatbelt sign went off , no-one of cabin crew walked down the aisle to check if pax were okay or needed anything. This was for over 30 minutes no sign of anyone in forward economy until the meal service. They ignored the call button that was kept on and refreshed for 25+minutes Toilets were not maintained clean. When asked to speak to person in charge .. aisle flight attendant said she was busy and ignored the request. Asked for green tea .. flight attendant never came back and when she passed and I asked again .. she said there was none and walked away. Headset was not working … after repeated requests to replace … finally after an hour it was replaced. On an 8 hour flight from Abu Dhabi to Mnl crew only came out during service and once to give water. Other than that they were not visible. Very disappointing experience with cabin crew as well as with check in staff at Riyadh airport. Service and attitude has slipped tremendously in dealing with economy passengers. What is happening to Etihad Airways?
route: Riyadh to Manila via Abu Dhabi

author: S Bahram
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   My baggage was damaged and after a long back-and-forth, their “final fair compensation” was only USD 50 or a travel voucher. Even worse, they closed the case and marked it as resolved despite my clear rejection of the offer and without my consent. I repeatedly contacted customer service, only to constantly hear “this is not our department” or “we cannot help you.” When I tried contacting the supposedly dedicated department via email, I was told the email address itself is inactive for claims handling. The irony is unbelievable — the department responsible for complaints apparently cannot even receive complaints.
route: Riyadh to Kuala Lumpur via Abu Dhabi

author: L Pan
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   40-hour delay, broken promises, and the disgrace of a 'Case Closed' without resolution. The ordeal began with flight EY871 on 20th December (HKG to AUH). Originally scheduled for 19:35, we were first told of a one-hour delay, which became four hours, before the flight was finally cancelled due to "technical problems." What followed was a complete failure in communication. Etihad only sent an email the following morning (21st Dec) rescheduling our flight to 12:30. This was seven hours earlier than the original daily schedule. The airline made zero effort to call or ensure we received this critical update. Had we not checked our emails at that specific moment, we would have missed the flight. To clear the terminal during the cancellatio, ground staff in Hong Kong instructed us to take a taxi home and promised a full refund of the expenses. Etihad has refused to reimburse the costs. The disruption continued on our return leg. Due to a delay from Casablanca, we missed our connecting flight to Hong Kong (EY870, scheduled for 31 Dec at 21:15). Instead of spending New Year's Eve as planned, we were stranded in Abu Dhabi and did not arrive home until 08:30 on 2nd January. Despite this 24-hour displacement on the return sector alone, Etihad has failed to provide an accurate Delay Certificate, preventing us from filing travel insurance claims. After four months of "investigation," Etihad’s only response was an insulting USD 200 travel voucher, which I have repeatedly refused.  They simply chose to stop responding.
route: Hong Kong to Casablanca via Abu Dhabi

author: C Maltin
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Horrible customer service. No help what so ever, hours on the phone to get assistance and any opportunity to charge extra fees. Then to board a plane and things in the seat broken. Choose any other airline. And charging extra for wifi after a ticket costing $7000
route: London to Sydney via Abu Dhabi

author: R Malders
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   I recently flew business class with Etihad Airways and had an overall strong and well-organized experience. From boarding to arrival, the service, comfort, and catering were of a high standard and clearly tailored to a premium product. The cabin crew was professional, attentive, and consistent throughout the flight, which made for a relaxed and comfortable journey. The quality of the food was good, with a balanced menu and well-presented food. I sat in seat 10A (window seat), which offered a pleasant experience in terms of comfort and space. At the same time, there are a few points that could be improved to take the experience to an even higher level. Seat privacy could be better, especially for passengers who value a more secluded and quiet environment in business class. Additionally, flexibility regarding transfers in the event of delays could be further improved. A more proactive and solution-oriented approach would enhance the customer experience. With a few targeted improvements in privacy and operational flexibility, this level could grow further from good to excellent. All in all, a very positive experience. I would recommend Etihad Airways for business class travel and am certainly considering flying with them again.  Ik heb recent business class gevlogen met Etihad Airways en overall een sterke en goed georganiseerde ervaring gehad. Vanaf boarding tot aankomst waren service, comfort en catering van hoog niveau en duidelijk afgestemd op een premium product. De cabinecrew was professioneel, attent en consistent gedurende de vlucht, wat zorgde voor een ontspannen en comfortabele reis. De kwaliteit van het eten was goed, met een gebalanceerd menu en verzorgde presentatie. Ik zat op stoel 10A (window seat), wat qua comfort en ruimte een prettige ervaring bood. Tegelijkertijd zijn er enkele punten die verbeterd kunnen worden om de ervaring naar een nog hoger niveau te tillen. De privacy van de stoelen kan beter, zeker voor passagiers die waarde hechten aan een meer afgesloten en rustige omgeving in business class. Daarnaast kan de flexibiliteit bij transfers in geval van vertragingen verder worden verbeterd. Een meer proactieve en oplossingsgerichte aanpak zou de klantbeleving versterken. Met enkele gerichte verbeteringen in privacy en operationele flexibiliteit kan dit niveau verder doorgroeien van goed naar uitstekend. Al met al een zeer positieve ervaring. Ik zou Etihad Airways aanbevelen voor business class reizen en overweeg zeker om opnieuw met hen te vliegen.
route: Amsterdam to Phuket via Abu Dhabi

author: E Valtoure
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |  Between Abu Dhabi and Lisbon, Etihad now uses a charter company, Hi Fly. A couple of weeks before our flight, we received an email informing us of this change. After checking, it appears that Hi Fly is not an airline but a charter company. The aircraft was an old A330, the crew was Portuguese. Basically, what you get is the level of a low cost airline for the price of Etihad. Old seats, almost non existent IFE: the large screen above your feet doesn't work, nor does the remote control (even for the lights). You need to use your own tablet and earset, scan a QR code hidden on the armrest, and get access to a list of maybe 10 movies, none of them worth watching. The crew was unprofessional and noisy (they all gathered in the front pantry to chat loudly, even with ear plugs I couldn't sleep). I complained to Etihad who couldn't care less. I had to press them to reply to me, which they finally did. Their position is that Hi Fly is their "trusted partner" and that I have no reason to complain. So, know it, between LIS and AUH, you will pay for Etihad and fly Low Cost. Of course, they play on the lack of alternative when you fly to the Far East from Lisbon. We will never fly Etihad again.

author: Richard Gregson
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   This is the worst experience I have ever had with an airline or travel company. The level of communication and assistance offered by Etihad after the US and Israel attacked Iran, disrupting airspace in the middle east, was non-existent. We had flown out to visit our son on the 19th February, a week before hostilities broke out. Due to fly home on the 7th March, our flight was first rescheduled earlier the same day and then cancelled 6 hours before take off. The only emails we received after that were Etihad trying to get get us to accept a refund for the return leg so they could cut us loose. We ended up having to book tickets home from Singapore via Tokyo 2 weeks later and £5000 more than planned. I can only imagine the situation some travellers found themselves in if they didn't have any spare cash. Terrible, terrible airline. In contrast, Japan Airlines and British Airways were superb (aside from charging £1600 each for a one way ticket home).
route: Manchester to Kuala Lumpur via Abu Dhabi

author: Ian Horrocks
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |  Etihad now add ridiculous charges after booking. I would not mind if they were transparent, but they are not. Customer service do not know the meaning of the word. It is very disappointing as they used to be one of the best. Would now describe them as a budget airline, other than their prices. In flight service also simply average. An extremely poor third when compared to Emirates and Qatar.
route: London to Bangkok via Abu Dhabi

author: Hussain Munniwala
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   We recently went through a horrific experience with Etihad Airways. The airline appears to be overbooking its flights. The experience begins when I attempted to check in online and the system refuses to allow me to do so. At the check-in counter, the staff politely refuse to issue my boarding pass and direct me to another counter for further assistance. The staff at that counter ask me to wait for 1–2 hours and say that if space becomes available, I  will be allowed to board the flight. At first, we (a group of four) thought this was just a one-off incident, after numerous arguments and discussions with third-party staff we were left with no option but to take the next available flight to Colombo the following day. They offered us hotel accommodation 30–40 minutes from the airport. Upon reaching the hotel around 3:00 a.m. we came to the conclusion that this seems to be a policy by Etihad to generate additional revenue. Therefore, please be very careful when choosing to fly with Etihad, especially if you are short on time or have a tight connecting flight, as there is a significant risk of being denied boarding.

author: S Karish
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Etihad’s A380 has inconsistent service standards on Indian subcontinent routes. If you are flying for the seat, you will be happy. If you are flying for a seamless, premium end-to-end journey, you may find the inconsistencies and upselling frustrating. On the YYZ–AUH leg, the cabin was exceptionally quiet, spacious, and the crew was highly efficient. However, the experience becomes fragmented on regional legs (AUH–COK). Service quality dipped significantly, and one crew member lacked the basic professional tact and sensitivity expected in a premium cabin. Beyond service, two major drawbacks hinder the experience. Compared to other major carriers, the Etihad app is insufficient. It lacks essential real-time luggage tracking, which is a standard expectation in 2026. Despite holding a premium Business Class ticket, the airline continues to play "upsell games" for seat selection. This nickel-and-diming is a low-cost carrier tactic that devalues their brand. While check-in at YYZ was straightforward, the boarding process in Abu Dhabi remains disorganized and needs streamlining to match the quality of the new Terminal A.
route: Toronto to Kochi via Abu Dhabi

author: F Sahita
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   On arriving at Frankfurt, I am informed my manual extension of German resident permit is not recognised in Abu Dhabi.  I wasn't able to board the flight but I met the boarding crew Alexander tried every means to help me get on the flight or at least the next one. I have never seen anyone try so hard to help someone, let alone a stranger. A gem of a person with empathy, kindness, patience, commitment and responsibility. Thank you so much Alexander, I appreciate your efforts.
route: Frankfurt to Bangalore via Abu Dhabi

author: A Thaha
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Extremely disappointing experience with refund process. I was promised a refund within 45 business days for a ticket booking due to a date mismatch. It's been over 3 months with no refund or clear update despite multiple follow-ups. Customer care was unhelpful and didn't provide any concrete solution.

author: Mahmod Abu hamed
review_text: Not Verified |  Very disappointing experience with Etihad Airways at the Phuket check-in counter. The service attitude was extremely unhelpful and unprofessional. The staff showed no willingness to assist or explain anything properly. This has nothing to do with the long waiting time — although the queue was the longest in the terminal with very few open counters — but everything to do with how we were treated. We were 1 kg overweight on our baggage amd were told we must pay 100 USD for excess weight. When we asked if we could remove 1 kg from the suitcase, we were told that we would need to leave the counter and rejoin the queue — meaning another 30–40 minutes of waiting. There was no flexibility, no effort to help, and no customer-oriented thinking. To make things worse, the staff members were whispering among themselves while looking at us, which felt disrespectful and unprofessional. Very disappointing customer service experience.

author: Alena Totskikh
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   We had a holiday planned from 10 to 15 January on the route Larnaca – Male via Abu Dhabi. We booked separate tickets: Larnaca–Abu Dhabi return with Wizz Air, and Abu Dhabi–Male return with Etihad (our first time flying Etihad). On 10 January, just as we were leaving our home to start the trip, we received a message that our Abu Dhabi–Male flight was delayed by 24 hours and moved to 11 January. This meant we immediately lost one full day of our very expensive Maldives vacation. After arriving in Abu Dhabi, we went to the Etihad Travel Desk. We spent around three hours speaking to a manager. We were told we were entitled to a hotel for one night and a small compensation. I specifically asked if we could rebook our return flights, because our holiday dates were fixed and we were losing a day. The manager said it was possible, but refused to do it at that moment, explaining that a long queue had formed behind us and he had to assist other passengers as well. We were taken by bus to the hotel. The next day (Sunday), we tried to find an open Etihad office in Abu Dhabi, but could not. At the airport, the queues were so long that we could not wait for our turn because we had to depart. We flew to the Maldives. There was no Etihad office there either. To avoid losing another day, we rebooked our return for 16 January instead of 15 January. As a result, we had to buy new tickets at our own expense: Male–Abu Dhabi and Abu Dhabi–Larnaca. I contacted Etihad customer support and explained the situation, including the overbooking and the fact that we had to pay for new return flights ourselves because the Travel Desk did not help when we asked. The response was extremely disappointing: Etihad refused any reimbursement, stating that the issue should have been solved at the Travel Desk. When I explained that the manager refused to assist at that time, I was told nothing could be done. This was a very stressful experience and a complete lack of customer care. I rate Etihad 1/10 and I will not fly with them again.
route: Larnaca to Male via Abu Dhabi

author: C Hewitt
review_text: Not Verified |  They exclude access to Lounges on the Business Value Fares. Guess its a one time for me.
route: Sydney to Milan via Abu Dhabi

author: Nadia Meyers
review_text: Not Verified |  As a result of missing our connecting flight in Kuwait with Kuwait Airways, we were compelled to stay overnight at a hotel in Kuwait. On the following day, contrary to our original booking, we were not transported onward with Kuwait Airways. Instead, without any consultation or our consent, we were rebooked onto a flight operated by Etihad Airways to Colombo. This flight was extremely chaotic and poorly managed. The overall level of service was unacceptable and had a significant negative impact on our travel experience. This matter is serious given that we have previously encountered substantial issues with Etihad Airways, which was the reason we had deliberately chosen not to travel with this airline again. Despite this, we were effectively compelled to fly with Etihad once more, resulting again in a negative experience.

author: Z Maqsood
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Don’t pay for the “change flight” option without reading the fine print very carefully. The flexibility is only valid for 4 months, is limited to a single change, and any additional changes incur extra fees. This information is not clearly disclosed elsewhere during purchase. On top of that, the fare difference charged for changes is almost as high as the cost of buying a new ticket, which defeats the purpose of paying for flexibility in the first place. Overall, the carrier feels disingenuous when it comes to hidden costs and lack of transparency. The experience left me feeling cheated, and it comes across as unprofessional and sleazy.

author: A Larkin
review_text: Not Verified |  Absolutely terrible experience. Delayed by two days - but it was the customer services and lack of care that let them down. Not interested in apologising, not interested in helping a family with children. They don't abide by basic care priniciples as laid out in their own charter. Horrendous compensation. I have traveled a few times now with Etihad and they are getting worse and worse. Food on plane was awful. ill thought out, stale bread. Small portions, treated like low class. Will avoid this airline at all costs next time as never want to deal with their dreadful customer services team who have no respect for people who have paid money. 12K to fly a family of 5 to Sydney and back and a really woeful experience from start to finish. Do better.
route: Sydney to London via Abu Dhabi

author: Andrin Koller
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   The absolute worst customer service available. They didn't let me board a flight because "I didn't have a visa". Turns out I didn't even need a visa for the country the flight was going to. I had to pay a second flight and then they told me I can't take the return flight previously booked together with the first "missed" flight because I haven't taken that one. Then they passed me forth and back between different customer support agents, "escalations" and random "airline policy" messages. Lastly, in the flight I ended up taking the food was bad even though I usually like airline food, the seats uncomfortable and the staff semi.
route: Zürich to Nairobi via Abu Dhabi

author: R Hardianis
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   I flew from Athens to Phuket via Abu Dhabi. On arrival at the airport in Athens, I didn't have access to the business class lounge. I didnt care, as by flight was early in the morning. On arrival in AbuDhabi went to the Guest Services and I was told that I need to get to the hotel they booked on my own. On arrival at the hotel, I was surprised to learn that it was a 4* hotel, and I had the most cheap room type available. Next day, I went to the breakfast lounge and I realized that my accommodation didn't include breakfast. On arrival at the airport after 2 days, again they asked for extra cash to enter the business class lounge.
route: Athens to Phuket via Abu Dhabi

author: Kayte Milcoy
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   A passenger in Manchester boarded our flight who had had nose bleeds and  we had to wait 2hrs for him to be removed from the plane this is classed as a medical offload meaning no compensation as they wipe their hands of any responsibility towards it! Not only did we have this drama we were crammed onto the world’s oldest plane where we had paid for extra legroom and had about a cm of space extra! The entertainment system didn’t work and when it came to land the couple in front still had their seats reclined staff did a quick once over the cabin but paid no attention or care to it. We landed in Abu Dhabi and had to stay over due to missing our connection, we waited nearly 2hours at the airport for our luggage as it had been sent to a connections zone and special requested to be returned to the belt and then a further 30 minutes for a taxi to the hotel where they put us….in the middle of nowhere and was undergoing renovations so was an absolute state! Once arriving home to express my concerns over there health and safety, lack of care and service they have washed their hands of us and closed the case, they don’t care what service they give you they just want your money.
route: Manchester to Tokyo via Abu Dhabi

author: Julia Franck
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   My flight from Melbourne to Abu Dhabi (flight EY 461 on 04/01/26) was delayed due to the late arrival of the aircraft. As a result of this delay, I missed my scheduled connecting flight from Abu Dhabi to Frankfurt, which was originally booked as a one-stop journey. I was rebooked by Etihad on an alternative routing via Zurich (EY 143), which converted my journey into a two-stop itinerary and included a layover of approximately five hours in Zurich. In addition, the rebooked flight to Zurich was delayed because flight preparations took longer than planned. Due to the combination of the initial delay, the extended rerouting, and the additional delay on the rebooked flight, I arrived at my final destination, Frankfurt, more than six hours later than my original scheduled arrival time (12:30 instead of 6:00am). I paid a higher fare specifically for a one-stop itinerary, and the rebooking significantly increased the overall travel time as well as expenses at the layover airport and inconvenience and expenses after arriving in Frankfurt due to missed train due to delay. I then contacted Etihad guest relations to request compensation or at the very least reimbursement for the costs incurred due to the delay and rebooked flight. After waiting a week for a response I received a response basically saying it's not their fault and I should use my insurance and that's it.  I could not recommend this airline, especially if you are traveling long distances do not expect good customer service.
route: Melbourne to Frankfurt via Abu Dhabi

author: T Kanyenko
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   My recent flight from Abu Dhabi to Russia left me deeply disappointed and shocked by how drastically Etihad’s standards have fallen. The flight was operated on an A320, a narrow-body aircraft that is unsuitable for such a long international route. Spending many hours in such a small cabin was extremely uncomfortable, inadequate ventilation, and stuffiness throughout the flight.  Flying such a long distance in a small aircraft for the same price as a full-service long-haul airline is not just uncomfortable — it feels humiliating. The situation was made even worse by the extremely poor and limited catering. Due to the heat and lack of proper ventilation, water was repeatedly distributed in small plastic cups instead of bottles, which further emphasized the level of cost-cutting and downgrade. After take-off, the cabin lights were never properly turned on. The entire flight was conducted almost in complete darkness. Even during meal service, only minimal night lighting under the panels was used, and later all lights were switched off completely.  During boarding, cabin crew attempted to collect hand luggage from passengers, including small cabin-size suitcases, claiming there was not enough overhead space. This caused tension and frustration. Only after objections from passengers were people allowed to keep their cabin bags. Both in Abu Dhabi and upon arrival, boarding and disembarkation were carried out via buses to a remote stand. Boarding was done in two separate bus loads. Travelling with multiple bags, this was physically exhausting and completely unexpected from Etihad Airways and a major international hub.  Etihad’s current “optimization” feels like a serious downgrade and an insult to loyal customers.

author: Carl Bengelsdorff
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |    My recent business class experience with Etihad Airways was, by far, the worst airline experience I have ever had. Even more disappointing than the flight issues themselves was the way Etihad handled the situation afterward, which was worse than what I have experienced with some low-cost airlines. Outbound Flight: Milan – Singapore (via Abu Dhabi) Abu Dhabi – Singapore The inflight entertainment system was not working. The compensation offered was close to ridiculous, and I was told on board that I could only receive it in the form of Etihad miles. Arrival in Singapore – Missing Luggage Upon arrival in Singapore, my luggage did not arrive. As a result, I spent 2 out of my 5 days in Singapore without my luggage. When I asked the Etihad lost-and-found agent how much I was allowed to spend on essential items, I was told that he did not know. This is unacceptable, as an airline should clearly inform passengers of the permitted expense limits. In the end, I was offered USD 50 for the delayed luggage, which I find almost offensive—especially considering that a business class passenger was left without luggage for nearly half of the trip. It also raises the question of how Etihad treats economy class passengers in similar situations. Return Flight: Singapore – Milan At check-in, I was moved from the window seat I had booked months in advance to a middle seat. Upon arrival in Milan, I discovered that my luggage was damaged, with personal belongings falling out. I reported the issue and later received an email from Etihad instructing me to visit the nearest authorized repair shop to obtain a damage assessment. The closest official repair shop is over one hour away, meaning Etihad expects me to waste half a day for something that should clearly be handled by the airline. More reputable airlines arrange for a courier to collect the luggage and return it repaired or replaced, without requiring the passenger to do anything. Poor Customer Service Follow-Up In total, I have sent 17 emails and 10 messages via Instagram. Every response has been the same: that Etihad is “looking into the matter.” More than two months have now passed without any resolution. I chose to try Etihad as I expect to travel extensively in that region in the future. However, this experience has been terrible in every respect, and I absolutely do not recommend Etihad to anyone. By far the worst airline I have flown with in the past 25 years.
route: Singapore to Milan via Abu Dhabi

author: N Garsen
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |  This feedback is yet another disappointing Etihad codeshare experience operated by Wamos Air, and raises serious concerns. Shortly after being seated and while passengers were still boarding, A flight attendant abruptly and aggressively removed two jackets from an overhead stowage compartment, declaring that this was “not allowed.” The jackets were thrown to the wrong passenger, creating confusion and embarrassment. The rightful owner, seated in row 40, then placed the jacket under his seat. The same flight attendant returned, stating, again loudly, that no items could be placed under the seat because it was an emergency row. The jacket was ultimately returned to the same overhead bin where it had been placed in the first place. The cabin crew displayed consistently rude and dismissive behaviour. No name badges were clearly visible or worn; where they were worn, the print was so small it was unreadable, making it nearly impossible for passengers to identify, compliment, or formally complain about a crew member. Midflight, when I approached the same flight attendant involved in the jacket incident and politely requested a coffee and a bottle of water, her response was dismissive: I was told to “go to the back and get it myself.” When I asked whether she was not serving passengers, she walked away without response. Cabin crew are the face of the airline, and this behaviour reflects a complete failure in service culture. The aircraft configuration was clearly outdated and poorly maintained, with: Broken TV monitors, Broken food trays, Broken seats, Lavatory drains becoming blocked mid-flight, No travel or location map on the inflight entertainment system and No Arabic language options on TV or radio. For an airline representing the UAE, the absence of Arabic content is unacceptable. Passengers could not even track their journey due to the missing flight map, an elementary inflight feature.  If Etihad intends to continue such partnerships, it has a responsibility to communicate that the experience will not match Etihad-operated flights.

author: L Kersen
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   The aircraft a WAMOS partner airline layout and cabin presentation did not align with Etihad’s premium brand expectations. Upon boarding, the air conditioning was not functioning, causing the cabin to become uncomfortably hot. This issue appeared to be addressed only after passengers began complaining, which is concerning. Passengers should never board an aircraft with a non-functional air conditioning system, nor should corrective action depend on complaints rather than proactive checks. The cabin felt more congested and cramped than typical Etihad-operated aircraft, and seating was uncomfortable. Crew members did not prepare seats adequately and did not offer assistance with Etihad seat covers, which further contributed to the feeling that this was not a standard Etihad experience. The crew, while professional in a basic operational sense, did not demonstrate the service excellence typically associated with Etihad cabin crew. The warmth, attentiveness, and proactive engagement that Etihad were largely absent. This distinction between Etihad crew and partner-operated crew was noticeable and detracted from the overall journey. The inflight entertainment system was non-functional during boarding and take-off. Once operational, the content offering was extremely limited, with only 39 movies available and none in Arabic, which is surprising and disappointing for an airline from the UAE. More concerning was the poor quality of the PA system, which was largely inaudible. In the event of an emergency, passengers must be able to clearly hear and follow crew instructions. This is not merely a comfort issue, it is a critical safety communication concern that must be addressed immediately. More than one hour into the flight, no drinks had been offered, making the service feel unusually slow. Additionally, the seatbelt sign remained on for extended periods, even during smooth flight conditions with no turbulence, unnecessarily restricting passenger movement. Once meal service began, I experienced good-quality food.  The aircraft, while operationally sound, showed clear signs of age and wear, including visible deterioration and duct tape holding panels together in the lavatory, which reflects poorly on cabin maintenance standards. The business class lavatory was clean and well-maintained, whereas the economy class lavatory was not, requiring cleaning before use.
route: Doha to Manila via Abu Dhabi

author: R Anthony Lerona
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   During this flight, the pilot did not provide any announcements apart from the arrival message, which was very difficult to hear due to poor audio quality. The flight attendants’ announcements were also unclear and not easily audible. Additionally, the cabin crew did not proactively offer water to passengers and mostly remained in the galley talking among themselves. When I requested water, the assistance felt reluctant and unwelcoming, as if it was an inconvenience to ask. Overall, the service made passengers feel uncomfortable rather than cared for.

author: Ahmed Issa
review_text: Not Verified |  Horrible experience.  I was forced to pay for 1 kg overweight per passenger although I have 4 checkin bags. Check-in was a chaotic, slow ordeal  Etihad ground staff were dismissive, stubborn, unprofessional, and unhelpful. No entertainment screens. Food was poor a sandwich handed over by hand. Seats were uncomfortable, toilets were dirty and not maintained. Flight time was accurate the only positive from Etihad. Overall experience was horrible and nowhere near the standard claimed to offer.

author: N Halena
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | The cabin crew were not very approachable or attentive, and their announcements were unclear. Overall cabin service fell below expectations. My checked luggage was placed on a second flight and arrived three days later, causing significant inconvenience. On a positive note, the pilot made enthusiastic announcements throughout the flight and spoke with a reassuring tone during turbulence, which was greatly appreciated.

author: L Calliaro
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |  I specifically booked a flight through Abu Dhabi because their system explicitly showed a hotel as available for my dates during the booking process. After taking my money, they refused to issue the voucher, claiming "blackout dates." This is bait-and-switch. They lure customers with the promise of a free stay, then deny it after the non-refundable flight is paid for. I paid a significant premium for a "Deluxe" fare to ensure flexibility. Etihad is now claiming that because one leg of the journey was "Basic," the benefits I paid for on the Deluxe leg are void. You cannot charge for a service and then unilaterally decide not to provide it.  Upon arrival in Abu Dhabi, I was left stranded. No assistance, no meal vouchers, and no accommodation was provided despite the long layover I was forced into by their system's false promises.
route: Bangkok to Rome via Abu Dhabi

author: L Leal
review_text: Not Verified |  My connecting flight to Abu Dhabi was delayed on 19th December 2025. Although my next flight to Bkk was rebooked by the airline, I never got a compensation for a hotel or food. It was a horrible  experience having had to stay at Abu Dhabi airport for 18 hours! The rebooking office was not very helpful either. I missed my paid one night hotel in Bangkok plus I spent money to stay in the airport lounge. Etihad Airways is the worst airline I've ever experienced.
route: Nairobi to Bangkok via Abu Dhabi

author: William Jackson
review_text: Not Verified |  Just an update on my nine month battle with Etihad Airways to try to obtain compensation after a disastrous experience. Flight booked with and paid in full to Etihad Airways from Barcelona to Da Nang via Abu Dhabi and Kuala Lumpur. I was denied boarding at Kuala Lumpur by Etihad's partner airline Batik Air Malaysia as they said I needed a visa to enter Vietnam. As a UK passport holder I didn't need said visa. After arguing the toss backwards and forwards with both airlines, Batik Air finally agreed that it was their error and they would reimburse me my extra expenses, some 850 dollars in all, provided Etihad Airways provided an RAA (Refund Application Authority). Etihad are refusing to provide this for some reason known only to Etihad. They really must be one of the world's worst airlines. They will certainly never see another cent from me.
route: Barcelona to Da Nang via Abu Dhabi

author: E Gale
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Never fly with this airline. We had an 18-hour flight, and Etihad staff confiscated our power bank that cost $100. We have traveled with this power bank many times, on different airlines and to many countries, and never had a single issue — only with Etihad. The power bank was not damaged, not defective, and fully compliant, yet it was simply taken away without any alternative solution. As a result, we lost $100 and were left without any power for our phones during an 18-hour flight. This is completely unacceptable and extremely frustrating. A long-haul flight without phone battery is not just inconvenient, it’s stressful. Very disappointing experience.
route: Seoul to Tel Aviv via Abu Dhabi

author: Rohith Jayawardene
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | While flying economy on the Dreamliner with Etihad is not an exceptionally pleasurable experience, in Business Class it's a whole other level altogether. Despite the 1x2x1 layout, I purposely chose a window seat, as it offers a little more privacy. I also do like the larger windows on the 787, although the blinds came down being on a night flight. The seat is exactly the same as in their A380s, fully flat for sleeping, with extra features like lumbar support, firmness and massage facility. The cabin crew on both flights were extremely professional and friendly, addressing me by name, taking my meal and drinks orders, and serving times (dine on demand service). I was also able to request drinks/cocktails not mentioned in the menu, which were perfectly blended and promptly served. From pre-departure drinks to dinner and breakfast, the service was attentive and on time. My only constant little gripe is about the E-Box IFE, which seems to have the same old stuff with little new additions. This could be, as I fly frequently with Etihad and am familiar with what's on. A couple of things were missing from my previous experiences - no turndown service anymore. However, the thin mattress provided was adequate, and I did get a couple of hours' sleep. The Espa Amenity Kit has the basic items, minus the cologne.

author: Rohith Jayawardene
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |  I have always enjoyed flights on the A380s, and especially the excellent cabin layout and on-board service. However, on my last two trips, there was a slight drop on the service front. On the outbound night flight, the cabin was full, and the dining had got to a poor start. After a long wait, pre-dinner drinks were served with nuts (not warm). I don't know whether there were fewer cabin crew, but the couple I saw were frantically pacing up and down to serve dinner. Following my starter, I had to wait for 35 minutes for the main course - Braised Beef, which was only slightly warm. The drink I requested with my meal was also forgotten. Moving to the small lounge later on, I was able to help myself to a drink, and coffee which was served promptly. Later on, I was also served with my favourite snack - the steak sandwich. The flight was comfortable in both directions, and I was able to get a few of hours of sleep. A couple of things I noticed have also changed. There was no 'Food and Beverage' service that you could directly order from the IFE (I was told that this was a temporary issue). The cold towels also did not come on a tray, instead it was provided in a small sealed pack, which lacks that personal touch. And one last thing - the amenity kit placed on my table had already been opened, and two items were missing.

author: S Gallo
review_text: Not Verified |    Horrible experience. Booked to try their stopover program, to get a reply just after a booked that they were fully booked in all their hotels. After ignoring all.my request, since wasn t anymore point for me to spend 75 hours in Abu Dabhi i ve been ask to pay over 300 usd of just penalty to change the flight to have a shorter layover. Costumer service horrible, and never will fly again
route: Bangkok to Rome via Abu dabi

author: C Hee
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |  Overall quite good. The seat, mattress and duvet were all copmfortbale. They offer dine on demand which is much more convenient. The cabin crew were very attentive.

author: Sandra Harb
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   They broke my husband’s TUMI luggage (it was even wrapped) and refused to compensate; There way a lot of incoming and outgoing emails with zero outcome; so unprofessional.

author: L Hee
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Disappointing airline. The flight started with a nearly three hour delay that caused significant inconvenience. The cabin crew was rude and not caring. The seat was good and they offer earplugs, eyemasks and lotion to passengers.

author: Summer Basharat
review_text: Not Verified |  I traveled through Etihad airlines from Colombo to Islamabad via Abu Dhabi along with my sister. Our flight was cancelled delayed and rescheduled several times, no food provided nor any hotel stay by Etihad. I am trying to contact through Etihad whatsapp but it's AI so system is replying regular systematic messages, Etihad chat is not accepting my name saying "invalid input", and no response from Etihad email. We are disappointed.
route: Colombo to Islamabad via Abu Dhabi

author: Dila Cuhadar
review_text: Not Verified |  This was genuinely the worst travel experience of my life. On what is supposedly one of their most popular flights, the airline overbooked by about ten passengers, and I was forced onto an alternative route that added 10 extra hours to my journey. I then had to wait at the transfer desk for three hours, along with dozens of other stranded passengers. People were crying, there was no water provided, and only two staff members were trying to handle what felt like around a hundred cases. The situation was completely chaotic and incredibly stressful. I’ve since started a claim regarding what happened, but so far no one has responded to me. Based on my experience, I will be telling everyone I know to avoid this airline at all costs.
route: Trivandrum to London via Abu Dhabi

author: Dhanoop Jose
review_text: Not Verified |  I booked a basic ticket from New York for January 8th with a return on January 18th. It was only days after booking that I realized the fare included only a 7kg carry-on. I had to pay an additional $200 for each leg for a checked bag. Lesson learned.
route: New York to Cochin via Abu Dhabi

author: Tomer Noiman
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | Had a terrible experience with Etihad. Food was Ok. However, the return flight was delayed, and ALL the luggage on the plane did not arrive at Tel Aviv. This was made worse when I was forced to check my trolley due to a lack of space on the flight. I arrived at Tel Aviv without a toothbrush or a change of underwear, and I had an extremely important conference the next morning. I bought everything I needed, assuming Etihad would reimburse me. Of course, I kept the invoices and filed a proper lost luggage complaint. The luggage arrived two days later. Then Etihad claimed I was not entitled to reimbursement because my luggage was eventually found, and I was in my home country anyway. It should be noted - I live in Eilat, not Tel Aviv. Telling me I don't deserve reimbursement because I was in my home country is like telling a New Yorker staying in Boston that they could just go home and pick up a change of clothes. It's a 4-5 hour drive. I canceled all future flights with the airline. Don't go for the low prices, they come with low-quality care.
route: Tokyo to Tel Aviv via Abu Dhabi

author: S Saiyed
review_text: Not Verified |  When flying with Etihad on a basic economy ticket, passengers are not allowed to bring any luggage for free. This means that if you want to bring a bag, you have to pay a fee of $200 for each one. My mother had to pay this amount when she traveled yesterday, but the receipt she received said it was for excess baggage charges, which was confusing. The staff member who helped us was very rude and unhelpful.
route: New York to Ahmedabad via Abu Dhabi

author: H Neitsen
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   After many years of flying Germany-Australia with Etihad we had to cancel tickets in 2022 due to a death in the family. Despite providing all the required documentation, hundreds of phonecalls, emails and chats later we still have not received the refund. Twice we were contacted to say that the refund had been approved if we send the documentation again which we immediately did. The constant reply over the years of "thankyou for your patience" is extremely frustrating. A warning to others whose plans may change, don't fly Etihad.
route: Frankfurt to Sydney via Abu Dhabi

author: J Harris
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Before booking, I contacted Etihad to confirm the Guest Miles needed to upgrade our Abu Dhabi to Sydney flight. Their live-chat team confirmed in writing that the upgrade for two passengers would cost 100,000 miles in total. Based on that assurance, I transferred the miles immediately. I acted exactly as Etihad told me to. Then Etihad quietly increased the requirement to 160,000 miles, without any warning or acknowledgment, and the customer service nightmare that followed was unlike anything I’ve experienced. Instead of owning their mistake, Etihad began an endless cycle of delays, avoidance and scripted replies; behaviour that felt deliberately designed to push me to the point of exhaustion. Across months of emails, messages, and social media DMs, I received nothing but the same lifeless automated line: “We understand that you are looking for an urgent update on your case. Rest assured the team is doing their best and will share the outcome with you once they have fully investigated it.” Different agents, different days, but always that identical, robotic message. It became painfully obvious that nobody was “investigating” anything. Nobody was reading the case notes. Nobody was acknowledging the written upgrade confirmation I was given. And nobody was willing to escalate or take responsibility. It was as if Etihad had one strategy: ignore the problem until the customer collapses from frustration. Because of Etihad’s deliberate delays, the upgradeable seats that were available at the time of the miles transfer disappeared. That delay had extremely real consequences. Etihad even credited the flight miles incorrectly; 3,753 instead of 8,750, forcing me to chase yet another avoidable error. And again: no explanation, no ownership, no urgency - just more empty reassurances that someone “was looking into it.” What stood out most was the complete absence of transparency. Etihad repeatedly attempted to reframe the issue as a matter of seat availability, refusing to acknowledge the core problem: Etihad gave a confirmed price, induced the transfer of miles, changed the rate afterwards, and then delayed so long that the original inventory disappeared. At no point did any staff member take a moment to understand what had actually happened. It felt like dealing with a brick wall programmed to say “we’re sorry for the inconvenience” without ever meaning it. Even when miles-upgradeable seats later became available on the return leg, Etihad still showed no willingness to offer even a modest gesture of goodwill.

author: R Karmatasan
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |    Traveling on my return flight from London to Bangalore via Abu Dhabi and ticket is booked on Etihad Airways. I discovered on the return flight back to Bangalore that the travel leg from Abu Dhabi to Bangalore will be on Akasa Air flight. The seat selection was not possible for this Abu Dhabi to Bangalore Akasa Air flight at the time of the check-in and I was told at London airport that they could not do it either due to the Akasa Air thing and that a middle seat was automatically allocated - which I hate the most. I was also told that the seat selection can be changed at the departure gate in Abu Dhabi. The flight was delayed by three hours and when the personnel arrived at the gate - not possible to change seats and the flight is full. The seats in the B737 max were very narrow and not fit for an international flight and being in the middle seat made it too squeezed.
route: London to Bangalore via Abu Dhabi

author: DESI Sumadio Madsedio
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   They gave us an unbelievably terrible experience. The ground staff in Madinah were arrogant, rude, dismissive, and unhelpful. We were traveling with a group for Umrah, including 11 family members, with a baby, young children, and elderly parents. They intentionally placed the baby far away from the parents, and the children and elderly were also scattered in seats far apart. When we asked for help to put us together, especially the baby and young kids, they refused to care at all. Only after we raised our voices and got angry did the airport manager finally step in to help. From check-in onward, every ground staff member acted arrogant and full of themselves, as if we were a burden. They behaved like we didn’t even pay for our tickets. Your entire business is nothing without customers. Show some respect and provide proper service. Even the cabin crew acted cold and detached, no warmth, no hospitality, nothing you would expect from a professional airline. I will never fly with Etihad again.
route: Madinah to Medan via Abu Dhabi

author: T Maston
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Everything happened on ground in AUH. Lounge crew assigned me for a gate change C38 at end of terminal. I double checked and it was confirmed so. When I reached that gate it was a flight to Lahore ! My flight changed again to gate B26 which is completely opposite the other site of the airport and far to reach. As a consequence I missed my flight and stayed in AUH for 7 h more! I confront ground staff with their mistakes but the only thing they do is say that it’s not their mistake and they assigned me for business class lounge again and have to wait. I will not recommend this airline.
route: Bangkok to Jeddah via Abu Dhabi

author: Tomas Ficza
review_text: Not Verified |    Even though I booked the flight well ahead they told me it was full and I can't fly. Every staff member at the airport told a different story and told me to go ask someone else. Shockingly, one member told me, that I should have paid for extra seats and I would be on the plane. Very unprofessional, noone knows what to do and I'm sitting at the airport waiting for some information.

author: M Reynolds
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   The flights left and arrived on time, but service from cabin crew was 1.5 star. They seemed to have no clue what even minimal polite service should be, and I don't think I saw any of them smile. I will happily pay more next time for a different flight experience.
route: Delhi to Atlanta via Abu Dhabi

author: Eva Rohlfes
review_text: Not Verified | We flew with Etihad this spring and our stroller got lost on the way back home. Since then, it took me several hours to fill out all the forms and evidence. They make it almost impossible for you to get to the point where they offer you a refund. I managed to get there, but even then there is no direct e-mail adress or a direct person you can contact. I had to use the chat on their homepage to get some information, but they never give you a direct e-mail adress. So I filled out the form with my bank details and signed it, but at the end I always get an error code, but the system doesn't show you what is the error. Now I get reminders every few days that I have to fill out the form, otherwise the refund link will expire. The Email adress is a no reply e-mail. When I wrote to the Feedback Email I got an e-mail back that no one will read it or reply. So I used the chat again and they told me, I should not worry and the manager of the claim will contact me. No one contacted me and there is no way to reach them. Of course they do this on purpose and hope that you will give up at some point. This kind of behavior should be forbidden by law. First they lose your stuff, then they make it impossible to get back your money for it. I have spent about 6 hours to try to solve it and it is still unsolved. My frustration is endless and I am so mad at them.
route: Singapore to Frankfurt via Abu Dhabi

author: J Kean
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Etihad lost the bags for the entire business class for two hours after landing. I had an Airtag in my bag, so I knew it was in Boston, and it just sat on the tarmac. There were no Etihad people to talk to, no one who would bring the bags the final 100 yards to the baggage claim, no one to say they were sorry. After traveling for 20 hours and paying for a a business class ticket that includes priority baggage, this was ridiculous. The level of service here is inexcusable. Etihad refused to offer even a discount on a future flight.
route: Doha to Boston via Abu Dhabi

author: C Marbin
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   We had a connecting flight from Osaka to Warsaw via Abu Dhabi, where upon arrival, our second connecting Etihad flight was delayed by an additional 5 hours. There were three of us, and it was the middle of the night. The airline only offered a meal voucher. We could sleep on the airport seats. Upon returning, I filed a complaint demanding compensation for EU law, which is €600 per person. The airline responded that they were outside the EU, only landed at an EU airport, and issued a $100 voucher. There was no further response to the complaint for days. Be aware that if you buy tickets with them, you will only receive a small handout in the event of delays.
route: Osaka to Warsaw via Abu Dhabi

author: Ritz Bayanin
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |    The flight was operated by Wamos Air. Cabin crew are not friendly! Skipped a meal for us and didn’t even apologise. Bathroom stinks! It seems like they are not cleaning and maintaining the cleanliness. If I only knew that this is not the real Etihad, I will not book a flight. There’s a very big difference between Wamos and Etiha. Such a poor service with Wamos air. Will never book this airline again.

author: Michael Britton
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Fantastic trip from LIS to AUH, excellent service. From AUH to BKK a nightmare. Had to beg for food and wine. Ordered breakfast but when I asked where it was, I was told it was 'too late' Problem with these airlines is they can treat you really badly, but there is no recourse.
route: Lisbon to Bangkok via Abu Dhabi

author: A Harsana
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |  My Etihad flight was delayed for more than 7 hours, causing me to miss my connecting flight. Despite being entitled to compensation under airline regulations, Etihad has been avoiding responsibility for over two months. I’ve received only repetitive automated emails asking to “check bank details,” even after providing verified information multiple times. On top of that, I faced rudeness and complete indifference from the airline’s staff during the delay. This experience showed an alarming lack of professionalism and respect for passengers.

author: H Nasulev
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |    Our flight was delayed over five hours, and despite being entitled under local law to accommodation and having written confirmation we were left stranded with no hotel and no real assistance. The customer service was shockingly poor. After submitting detailed feedback about the lack of hotel accommodation, the lack of support, the airline ignored all of it and simply closed the case without addressing any of the issues.
route: Seychelles to Tel Aviv via Abu Dhabi

author: L Han
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   First time flying Etihad and will be last. As others have stated the delays and service are simply awful. Our flight was delayed by 3.5 hours for a less than 1 hour flight. According to flight aware the plane has not left the previous destination when we checked in but it wasn't until about 2 hours to boarding that I received an email for the delay. After reaching new gate assignment there were no Etihad personnel other than an agent from previous flight. About 100 passengers were waiting and asking for clarification but none was given other than it's delayed. That agent received tons of pressure from pissed off passengers although not warranted but justified given Etihad never sent a qualified agent or supervisor but simply let passengers to fend for themselves. Mind you this is at AUH their home hub and there are no planes substitute for the short 1 hour flight which is hard to believe. Not to mention the number of personnels walking, talking and sitting around through terminal and no one cared or told to do anything.
