Eventually I spoke to someone who directed me to the transfer desk for more information. Now the transfer desk is OUTSIDE security how idiotic can you be to direct passengers there. When I did reach the desk there were about 100 people in line and another 100 people in the room waiting. What a ridiculous setup and direction. Gave up and went through security again in case the flight got moved up and received another email the Etihad will compensate for food and drinks. No instructions on how to use and still no one around cared to explain what and how to redeem. Since I've already spent my own time and money to purchase items the compensation was too late. After chatting with Etihad agent online was told able to redeem at food court so decided to test. The closest vendor said food orders will take 30+ mins as many are ordering. So I inquired about the premade sandwiches in case and she said they they are not of the reimbursement. Then I asked for a bottle of sparkling water and again was told only some soda and juice are allowed. Instead of typical $10 to use Etihad has the process where it's almost impossible to redeem. The food agent felt sorry that I wasn't able to redeem for anything I asked decided to give me the bottle as I'm not asking for food. If Etihad agents would simply get off their butt and face passengers to offer assistance they will understand the situation like the food vendor. But instead they chose to let others deal by sending passengers other way. Also the food vendor never asked for my boarding pass like the Etihad email stated as she clearly senses the emotion knowing I'm not some guy from a different flight looking for free food and drinks. They should look at their neighbor Qatar for improvements.

author: D Bawtir
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Worst customer service ever. Flight from Melbourne got delayed and I knew we will miss our connection to Munich. Talking to the ground staff in Melbourne they kept reassuring me that I will make the connection (and same in the airplane after asking multiple times before landing). During the layover we had to wait 12 hours (after a 13 hours flight and 1 hour delay). The airline offered to give us a hotel room. But, the hotel is outside the airport and we needed a visa to get out. Instead of being flexible and giving us a room in the airport's hotel, they took our passports and made us wait 7 hours only to tell us we did not get a visa. During those 7 hours I talked to all representatives in the airport and at the call center. No one would reason with me and agree to grant us access to the lounge or airport hotel.  At 9 am, after being so insistent they agreed to finally give us a room at the airport's hotel. So, it was actually possible to do so.
route: Melbourne to Munich via Abu Dhabi

author: Bart Nanya
review_text: Not Verified | My parents wanted to change their flight to a few weeks earlier. I went on the Etihad website, and everything went smoothly — I could easily arrange it myself. I found a flight, and that’s the one we agreed to book. The price difference was about €450 in total — that’s after subtracting the value of the original tickets, adding the fare difference and the rebooking fees. So for two people, the total came to around €450 or slightly less. When I went to continue to the payment page, I noticed that my mother’s surname had one extra letter by accident. Before paying, I decided to contact Etihad through chat, and they were able to fix it for me right away. That part went smoothly. After that, I tried again to rebook the flight — and that’s where the problems started. The website kept giving error messages saying I had to contact support or try again later. I waited and tried again several times, but it just didn’t work. I also chatted with Etihad, but that was difficult because the chat system somehow stopped letting me connect with an agent. I waited until the next day, thinking maybe it was just busy. I had already cleared my cache and browsing history, as they later told me to do, but nothing worked. The next day, I tried again — still the same error. I even tried on other browsers, on my phone, on a laptop, and on another laptop — always the same error message. Now, 24 hours later, I finally managed to speak to a live agent again. I got through by asking different questions in the chat. The agent was able to find the same flight I had tried to rebook earlier. But now, suddenly, it wasn’t €450 anymore — the rebooking cost had jumped to €1100. That was strange, because they’re supposed to subtract the value of the original ticket from the new one. The agent said, “Yes, but it’s still €1100.” That would mean the new tickets would have to cost around €1700 in total, which didn’t make sense. I quickly checked on Skyscanner and found the exact same Etihad flight for €1000 total for two people — not €1100. I pointed that out, but the agent just said, “I don’t know either. This is the price difference I can offer you.” I said that was strange, because the ticket became 2.2 times more expensive in only 24 hours. She kept repeating that there was nothing she could do. Its weird that she also said that the price was adjusted with our old tickets while a new ticket is even cheaper than the adjusted price. I am really, really disappointed in Etihad, and I honestly wouldn’t recommend anyone go through this process. You get taken advantage of right in front of your eyes. how is this even allowed. I personally fly a lot with my family and will never ever fly with Etihad ever again.

author: Samir Garg
review_text: Not Verified | I had booked a flight for my wife from Mumbai to London on Etihad Airways for the 3rd of October & return on 13th of October. The fare booked did not have a check-in luggage included & nowhere on their website were we able to add the check-in luggage. On contacting the airline, we were told that the check-in luggage cannot be added in advance & we will need to do the same at the counter. On enquiring about the cost, we were told that the cost for the luggage would be max. 200$.  On reaching the counter for the Check-In, we were informed by the staff that it will cost us Rs. 55,000/- (USD 650$) for check-in bag weighing 20 Kgs. This was ridiculous, but even after arguing with their manager for an hour, they did not even budge and we had to pay that amount. Next day I talked to Yatra & my travel agent to cancel the return flight so that I can book another flight, but was informed that the cancellation fees is 100% & I will not get any refund, nor can I upgrade the ticket to a higher class which will include the luggage.
route: Mumbai to London via Abu Dhabi

author: S Marney
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   I wish I had read the reviews. Was absolutely surprised to see that lounge access is not allowed to Business Class passengers. First experience traveling in Business Class for last 30 years. The crew was very polite but not professional. Service was less than poor.
route: Toronto to Bangkok via Abu Dhabi

author: P Hayne
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | This airline sells business class tickets without lounge access. So really this is an over priced premium economy product. ($11500aud). Food choice mediocre, service slow, bleak 777 cabin. I would expect more for my money. Will not fly with this airline again.
route: Sydney = to Manchester via Abu Dhabi

author: A Takla
review_text: Not Verified | Our experience with Etihad was nothing short of terrible. Our flight from Lisbon to Abu Dhabi was delayed, which caused us to miss our connection to Melbourne. Even though we arrived at the gate about 20 minutes before boarding closed, the ground staff were dismissive and unhelpful, telling us we had already been re-routed and could not board without our bags. Their lack of care and unwillingness to assist was appalling. We were then rebooked on a flight to Singapore, which was also delayed, leaving us scrambling yet again to make our next flight. Thankfully, Singapore Airlines handled the situation with professionalism—meeting us at the terminal, escorting us to our connecting flight, and even delivering our baggage (which Etihad failed to transfer) to us the following day. The contrast could not be clearer: Singapore Airlines went above and beyond, while Etihad failed at every stage—delays, poor communication, and complete lack of customer care. What was once considered a first-class airline has clearly deteriorated. I will not fly Etihad again, and I strongly advise others to avoid them as well.
route: Lisbon to Melbourne via Abu Dhabi

author: C Hamarty
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   No wheelchair was available at AUH despite pre-booking. As I have very low connection time, I have to walk a lot which was very painful for me AUH-CCU is code shared with Air Arabia. I was told that I will be provided meal, but no food was provided. In JFK-AUH sector, seat was very uncomfortable.
route: New York to Kolkata via Abu Dhabi

author: S Dawson
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | I want to take a moment to express my appreciation for the exceptional service I received from the Etihad staff at Dublin Airport today. From the ticketing counter to the boarding area, the entire team displayed high professionalism and customer service. I encountered a staff member named Bradley at the check-in area, who exemplified excellence in her role and followed all necessary protocols. In the boarding area, I had the pleasure of interacting with Reji, who was instrumental in addressing my inquiries and assisting me and fellow travellers. I am grateful for the opportunity to share this positive experience as a gesture of thanks for the outstanding efforts of the Etihad Airlines team. Their dedication enhances the travel experience for all passengers and highlights the importance of exceptional customer service in the aviation industry.
route: Dublin to Abu Dhabi via Colombo

author: S Gerner
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |  Etihad service is getting worse and worse. Several times we traveled with Etihad. It was ok in the past. But it is the 2nd time that my flight back from Jakarta is cancelled and changed. The first time it was ok as there was a convenient option. But this time? The flight has been cancelled and changed to be 20h earlier with 9h layover in Abu Dhabi instead of 2h. Our flight from Bali to Jakarta with Air Asia had to be cancelled. Alternatives??? Stop in Abu Dhabi and Rome? This was the last time with Etihad!
route: Jakarta to Munich via Abu Dhabi

author: Ehud Skolnik
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | Etihad Airways: A Warning to All Travelers Don't let the "luxury" lie fool you. My wife and I just finished a nightmare experience with Etihad, proving that paying for business class doesn't buy you a shred of accountability. We are sharing our story so you don't make the same mistake. From a two-day baggage delay on our outbound flight to two completely destroyed suitcases on our return, our trip was ruined. But the real insult? The way Etihad’s customer service handled it. Etihad's playbook for avoiding responsibility: Claiming "Minor Damage": A professional luggage repair service told us our suitcases were beyond repair. Etihad’s agents repeatedly insisted the damage was "minor." This isn't just a lie — it's a deliberate attempt to dismiss a legitimate claim. They sold us a premium ticket and left us with useless luggage. The Impossible Demand for Receipts: Etihad demanded we provide the original purchase receipts for bags we’ve owned for years. This is a transparent, ridiculous tactic designed to make it impossible for us to be compensated. Insulting Compensation: After weeks of being ignored, we were offered a pathetic $100 for two destroyed suitcases and for the two-day delay. As if that wasn't bad enough, they offered a useless flight voucher — a credit we will never use because we will never fly with Etihad again. Etihad Airways has proven they have zero respect for their customers, especially those who pay for a premium experience. Their refusal to provide a fair resolution and their disgraceful tactics are a clear warning to everyone. This isn't a minor issue; it's a systemic failure of customer service. We have exhausted all attempts at a reasonable resolution. Consider this a public service announcement: Don't be fooled by the fancy branding. When things go wrong, Etihad Airways will not stand by you. They will lie, evade, and insult you until you give up. We refuse to.
route: Tel Aviv to Phuket via Abu Dhabi

author: Ajaypal Singh
review_text: Not Verified | Paid 1200 extra for extra leg room “deluxe” economy seats but was told the only way I can get them is if I have my 5 y and 7 y old children sit separately in middle seats away from me. If we wanted the kids to sit with us, only regular economy seats are available. Not sure how a 5 yo can fly 13-14 hours alone. The help desk was of absolute no help. Basically fly economy while we charged you extra for so called “deluxe economy”. Never flying with them again.
route: Delhi to Chicago via Abu Dhabi

author: H Irving
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | The main disappointment was the ground crew, who destroyed the electric wheelchair we checked in from Tokyo and picked up in Warsaw, with a change of flights to Abu Dhabi. The wheelchair we picked up at the final airport was broken, wrapped in strings, with clips attached to the wheelchair's securing straps in the cargo hold. A complete lack of professionalism and respect for other people's property, especially for a wheelchair for a disabled person who needs one. The flight itself was relatively okay, but that was mainly due to the excellent airport staff at Tokyo and the decent service on board. Regarding the meals, I was also very disappointed because they offered a vegetarian option or chicken with rice. Wi-Fi was available on one flight, but stopped working after a while. A month earlier, on a flight in the opposite direction, the screen and entertainment system in my seat weren't working, so the flight attendant recommended contacting Etihad after landing to file a complaint. A month has passed since I filed my complaint, and Etihad hasn't responded. Overall, I'm very disappointed with Etihad Airways and I don't intend to repeat this experience on another flight. There are many other airlines with better customer service than Etihad.
route: Tokyo Narita to Warsaw via Abu Dhabi

author: Martin Ligas
review_text: Not Verified |    Compared with other middle easter airlines Etihad seem to be a budget option, providing basic amenities to sustain their brand. We flew with Etihad last year, where during our stop in Abu Dhabi our connecting flight got delayed for over 7 hours and with the exception of a water there was nothing the airline offered to their customers. Ad hoc live customer support is basically non existent. You can chat with bots or human operators that behave like bots and give you basic excuses but not a real assistance. This year a similar story occurred once we had issues with our loyalty program membership. One can just write emails that are left without reply or use a useless chat option that lets you connect with a human being after an hour waiting. And you won't get much of help. As a carrier they might be ok, but once it gets to issues do not count on getting any assistance.
route: Vienna to Bangkok via Abu dhabi

author: Thomas Corrigan
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | I decided to fly with Etihad Airways. Never again will I do this and I want to warn others of their incompetence and neglect. My original flight plan was meant to take 16 hours. With Etihad it took over 50 hours and they lost my luggage. I booked with Etihad Airways to get me to Johannesburg airport in South Africa, from London Heathrow, with a 2 hour stop in Abu Dhabi. I paid a lot of money for this flight, over £1100. The flight left Heathrow on time and as the flight landed in Abu Dhabi they announced some passengers connecting onto Johannesburg needed to wait for assistance. I was met by an Etihad worker who instructed me I was being removed from the flight, the connection to Johannesburg that I had booked and paid for, because they had over booked the flight! How is this possible? I had to make my way to a hotel and stay there for two nights before they could book me on to the next flight to Johannesburg (which they didn’t, they instead sent me to a different country). THATS NOT THE WORST PART. After already losing a day of my holiday I had discovered Etihad Airways had booked me onto another flight but instead of flying me to Johannesburg, which was my original plan, which I had paid for, they instead sent me to Nairobi, Kenya, with a connection from Nairobi to Johannesburg. But guess what? They delayed this flight to Kenya by 3 hours, leaving me waiting in the airport with no help or assistance. In addition, this delay caused me to miss my connection in Nairobi, Kenya. Etihad left me in Nairobi airport for 7 HOURS with no food and no water, as well as no assistance or help. I got a lovely email stating they wanted to fly me to Dar es Salam, Tanzania and then on to Johannesburg. After hours of back and forth I managed to find a helpful lady who went above and beyond and booked me on a direct flight to Johannesburg. Why couldn't Etihad airways have done this?! My chaos was not over yet. After finally reaching Johannesburg over 50 hours later, Etihad airways had lost my luggage. I lost 3 days of my holiday being flown around by this incompetent airline. They finally found my bag and returned it to me 2 days after landing in Johannesburg. I strongly recommend you DO NOT fly with this airline. If this was an elderly person, or a family, I dread to think the stress this would have caused them. The airline has not been in touch, nor compensated me for any of my delays, or kicking me of my first flight when they overbooked. Its a disgrace and I want to warn others. Etihad you're a disgrace.

author: R Vish
review_text: Not Verified | I had a flight booked from Abi Dhabi to LHR. During online check-in I was randomly assigned a middle seat (seat 47J). I paid extra money on their app to move to an aisle seat (seat 70C) as I had some pain in my legs and needed the space to stretch out. Etihad took the money from my account to move seat. When I got to the boarding gate, they issued me a boarding pass with my original, free, randomly assigned seat (seat 47J) and told me there must have been a glitch with the booking system as seat 70C had already been taken. I submitted a refund request to the feedback email address immediately after landing, but they are refusing to refund me. I've called the complaints number numerous times and have just been told there is nothing they can do, claiming I "was given a seat in the same cabin as the one I paid extra for so its not their fault"? They've literally scammed me and when confronted just shrug their shoulders and say there is nothing they can do. I would give them 0 stars if I could.

author: D Davis
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | Its not a premium brand. If you go with that mind set then its fine. Else you are into a bad experience. From booking ticket to onboarding everything ended up a nightmare for us and finally decided we will not be flying through Etihad again. Most worrying part is the biggest brand, represents a country. Does it means the business is not over all good ?

author: A Barkila
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Our flight was postponed by 24 hours about a week before our vacation, which meant we had to book a new hotel, new transfers to the airport, etc. We were offered the choice of either taking the flight or canceling it. Since we had no other choice, we had to accept the new flight. At the same time, we were told to document the additional costs we incurred and then contact customer service. Spoiler alert: It didn't help us, because the explanation was, well, you accepted the flight, so there's nothing to compensate. So far, so good. So we flew back home and lo and behold: two of our suitcases were badly damaged (see pictures). We went straight to the counter to get official confirmation of the damage. We got confirmation of the damage and at that point had no idea how long it would take to resolve the issue. We were required to obtain an evaluation from a luggage manufacturer stating that the suitcase could be repaired or was irreparable. We drove to a luggage manufacturer and obtained an evaluation for €25. We weren't surprised to learn that the suitcase couldn't be repaired because the damage was too extensive. We submitted the claim and after a few days received a message saying that we would either receive $50 by bank transfer as compensation or $75 store credit, as we hadn't uploaded a proof of purchase for the suitcase. Quick side note: The airline only allows (as far as I remember) 4 uploads on the platform, which makes it extremely difficult to upload all the evidence for the claim at once. A full refund would only be possible if we uploaded the original receipt. We bought the suitcase at a small outlet on our 2024 trip to Japan and had to search for the proof of purchase for hours in old documents. We were very happy when we found the proof of purchase (29,000 yen / about 169€) and uploaded it and the evaluation again. We rejected the offer. It didn't take long for the next email to arrive, again requesting the purchase receipt and offering us $50. We thought to ourselves: Maybe they didn't see the purchase receipt in the uploads. So we called and worked with customer service on the phone to ensure that the responsible employee received the documents. Now everything was done, now we would definitely get our money back, but unfortunately we were wrong, because the next email arrived a few days later. The proof of purchase had to be “itemized” and only then could full compensation be paid out. So we spoke to customer service again and made it clear that we had already uploaded the proof of purchase. It felt like Groundhog Day, because a few days later another email from our case handler followed: The purchase receipt must be “itemized” for full compensation, and this is the final compensation offer of $50 or $75 store credit. When we read this, we fully understood what was happening: the purchase receipt we had received, the only one we still had from our trip in 2024, the only one we had ever received and had struggled to find, was not enough for our case handler. It is not “itemized” enough for him: the purchase price, the name of the suitcase company, the date, the time, the name and address of the store in Shibuya, the change money we got back. None of that is enough for him. Maybe he wants us to go back to Shibuya and get a new one? I will not recommend this airline to anyone.
route: Osaka to Frankfurt via Abu Dhabi

author: A Hassen
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   As i wait in Muscat airport after 4 times getting my flight rescheduled. Their app shows that the flights latest update is at 23:50 while the screen at the airport is showing 22:25 and when i went to their helpdesk, the useless guy over there could not even provide any update. When i asked him which time is the correct one, he said : I don’t know. 4hours of delay for a 1hr trip.m. They decided to save some money by removing the screens from the airplanes and replaced them with the EBox that never works because the inflight internet doesn’t work. The flights are so packed that you can barely fit your legs. I am an Etihad gold guest and i am sorry to say that Etihad became now, in my opinion, the worst carrier that should be stripped from the title of being the national carrier of UAE.

author: Luca Anselmi
review_text: Not Verified | I fly the Rome–Abu Dhabi route on average 25 times a year, and no matter which class I travel, Etihad offers a level of hospitality and care that no other airline can match.

author: David Houlihan
review_text: Not Verified |   Yet another poor review I am afraid for Etihad to join what appears to be the " norm:" looking at the other reviews. Having been a Gold member for over 14 years I have see the ups and downs of this once Iconic brand. Marketing bling versus reality is now the norm. To be brief the latest flight DUB - AUH in Business. An old tired, retro B777 aircraft is always used on the AUH-DUB route. Seat was filthy dirty - previous passengers ear plugs( clearly used) food all over the seat and floor, empty used packaging stuffed down the seats, used socks stuffed into the side of the seat. I used a number of wipes to clean the seat and surroundings which came out black with dirt. Service slow, staff cutting is obvious and they are overwhelmed - how basic is to get a pre ordered glass of wine with your meal and not have to request it a number of times? sloppy, very young crew who had to bring other colleagues from Economy to help and step in and serve. The menu if it was costed I would say cost no more than 12 euro to produce and the wines are bottom shelf. Do not charge 20,000 AED if you simply can't deliver. I have said this again and again - Etihad continue to overprice consumers originating from AUH with prices double that of Qatar Airways and frankly do not deliver. So like many Abu Dhabi residents, I will use Qatar Airways and get a better, consistent product at a competitive price even with the added inconvience of having to transit.

author: P Deane
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   We bought our tickets in January for July travel. 4 of us in total from NRT to ATH via AUH. Due to aircraft change they downgraded 2 of us on the AUH to ATH leg. (3rd one only got a seat at the very last minute). There are no communications or alternatives, they should know well in advance if they overbooked, we only find out at the check-in in NRT that we are on standby and to "talk to the staff at the gate". To add insult, they offer a voucher for so call compensation that we can use for future flight or cash in. To cash in, we need to contact the call centre who will then generate a stupid link for us to input our bank details. They should refund directly to the original form of payment, what kind of poor practice is this? It's August and we are still waiting for the cash to show up in our bank. Such a low cost carrier approach. Their customer service online (chat and feedback form) are pretty poor too, you need to be a man for them to respond respectfully, if you are a woman they dismiss your message.
route: Tokyo to Athens via Abu Dhabi

author: S Tomasulo
review_text: Not Verified |   Flight EY079 on 25 May 2025 was delayed over 5.5 hours due to weather in India, arriving in Milan after midnight on 26 May,  long after public transport had stopped. I incurred $300 AUD in taxi costs. I approached Etihad’s ground staff in Abu Dhabi for assistance or alternative options, and they  refused to help. I was given was to complete an online feedback form. I submitted it multiple times, only to receive identical, generic no-reply emails each time — clearly automated — offering a $100 USD Etihad travel voucher. There is no way to reply, escalate, or speak to a real person. I accept that delays happen. But what defines an airline is not its glossy marketing, but how it treats passengers when things go wrong. In my case, Etihad demonstrated zero compassion, zero accountability, and no real customer support.
route: Sydney to Milan via Abu Dhabi

author: Arina Cherchik
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | I am shocked and deeply disappointed by the way Etihad handled my flight delay. My connection was delayed by almost 6 hours, and Etihad staff in Abu Dhabi openly admitted that the delay was their fault — not due to weather, not due to any external cause. Still, they refused to provide proper care or compensation. I had to pay €170 out of my own pocket for a hotel inside the airport to get some rest, and €50 for food since the only thing Etihad provided was a “meal” consisting of two eggs and a glass of cola. Yes — for nearly 6 hours of delay, they claim this is “enough”. On top of that, because of this delay, I missed important evening plans and had to rebook a hotel and pay for a taxi upon arrival, which I wouldn’t have needed otherwise. Total chaos, totally on Etihad — and they just shrugged and said it’s not their problem. This was not my first flight with Etihad — but definitely the last. The way they treat their passengers with such indifference and arrogance is absolutely unacceptable for an airline that claims to be premium. Etihad, if you want to call yourself a 4- or 5-star airline, start by treating stranded passengers like human beings — not like cattle.
route: Zurich to Moscow via Abu Dhabi

author: Zahid Islam
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Etihad has recently disappointed me continuously and I will never fly with them again. As a silver member, I no longer receive a different type of Welcome back greeting from the crew. I no longer have a crew member come looking for me during the flight and get asked if everything is alright and if I need anything. The food in economy is terrible and they have also become stingy and the bare minimum amount of food is served. Your tissue is also your napkin! The Etihad lounge at Abudhabi is equally bad. The same food gets prepared everyday. For breakfast, they were serving South Indian food for some reason! Stopover programs only includes Premier Inn now. Previously, I stayed at WTC Marriott. It is a shame but Goodbye Etihad.
route: London to Muscat via Abu Dhabi

author: C Mee
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   My family flew with them end of June with all 3 of us in business class. Not only did they change our flight timing twice (with once close to the departure date and no email informing us of the flight change), they also lost one of our checked in luggage. After lodging the lost baggage report at the airport, numerous chaser emails and chats, it took them more than 28 days to say it was not their problem and that I should have bought travel insurance.  My fault for believing I paid for a premium product and got treated like I was on a budget airline!
route: Singapore to Lisbon via Abu Dhabi

author: Michael Magerkurth
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | Chaos and nonsense. I had one fantastic team member, but everything else on this leg of my flight was way under my expectations of value for money, and value paid for a Business Class ticket. In the fantastic lounge it was announced that boarding would start, from the lounge, from the second floor, then the nonsense started. No crew/staffing, no direction, no  help, no signage. I asked for guidance, none. Then boarded, no help, no kindness, no service...until one staff member noticed my frustration 1.5 hours into the flight. I explained that previous members had promised help and been changed around. I talked to the purser, he said there would be a report, customer service, nothing. I called, wrote and got even more promised....we will check on this. Very poor experience, very poor communications.

author: Erhan Gogebakan
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |  Etihad ruined the first 2 Days of our honeymoon. On July 21, 2025, we were supposed to fly from Istanbul to Abu Dhabi on flight EY544, then connect to EY414 to Phuket. Due to a delay with EY544, we missed the connecting flight — it departed without us. We were stuck in Abu Dhabi for 1 night and 2 full days, losing the first 2 days of our honeymoon. T They only provided a hotel in Abu Dhabi, but there was no real compensation, no sincere apology, and no effort to make up for the time we lost. I contacted Etihad by email multiple times and asked, at the very least, to postpone our return flight by 2 days so we could recover part of our lost time — but there was no helpful response. I expected much better from an airline like Etihad. This experience has been hugely disappointing, and I feel completely ignored as a customer.
route: Istanbul to Phuket via Abu Dhabi

author: E Balsayen
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |  Avoid this airline at all cost the customer service is terrible. They don’t care about the well-being of their customer me and my two daughters 11 and 12 years old we’re scheduled to fly to Beirut with the news of a war breaking out I reached out to reschedule or cancel my flight or get a credit for future bookings. I emailed and called over and over again never received a response was not allowed to speak to a supervisor while. Absolutely no customer service
route: Chicago to Beirut via Abu Dhabi

author: Rana Alsaleh
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   On May 2, 2025, my 73-year-old mother traveled in Business Class with Etihad Airways. What should have been a comfortable flight turned into an ordeal that has been both shocking and infuriating. During the flight, my mother’s phone became stuck between the seats. She informed the cabin crew, who made an attempt to retrieve it but were unsuccessful. Instead of ensuring the phone was safely returned to her, the crew instructed her to leave the aircraft without it, assuring her that it would be located and returned on the plane’s next trip to Toronto. This was a deeply concerning decision, but it only got worse from there. My elderly mother was traveling alone, did not speak English, and was left stranded at the airport without her phone, without any contact information, and without anyone to help her. She was unable to reach me or anyone else in a foreign country.  Losing the phone wasn’t just inconvenient, it posed a serious privacy and security risk.  We submitted a Lost and Found report immediately after the flight and followed up multiple times via phone and email. After two months of waiting and hearing nothing, we finally received an email on July 8, stating that after contacting the crew and the maintenance team, the phone was not found on the aircraft. This response is unacceptable. Etihad made promises, gave false hope, and then simply failed to take responsibility. There has been no apology, no compensation, and no real effort to rectify the situation.

author: Melissa Wade
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Terrible flight. Booked a premium economy flight (extra legroom) with Etihad. Flight was to be operated by Etihad at time of booking. Discovered at Madrid airport that the flight was to be operated by Air Europa and that seats with extra legroom were unavailable. Sat in a seat with no legroom, not an aisle as booked for 6.5 hours on an overheated plane with grumpy Aireuropa staff. Made a complaint to Etihad post flight. No compensation or apology. Apparently it’s all in the fine print on the booking that you can pay extra for legroom on an Etihad flight and end up with none on an Air Europa flight. Don’t be fooled. I’ll never fly with them again.

author: R Karsen
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   What an abysmal experience. The airplane was a very old 777-300 with an outdated inflight entertainment system. The touch screen had a 2cm discrepancy and could not be used by touch. The remote did work, but not very well. The seat recline was super hard to manage. The food was fine, and they did 2 services on a 6hr flight. The cabin staff was severely lacking. Next to me sat a passenger with a horrendous bodily odor. We sat four abreast; husband, child, wife and me. I spoke to the cabin staff and they told me the flight was fully booked so they could not reseat me. Okay, too bad. I then asked if they could talk to the passenger about her odor, or perhaps ask her to switch places with her husband. The cabin staff refused to help me. They told me its forbidden by Etihad/Senior Purser to confront passengers in these situations.  Its appalling to be treated like that, what a poor show.
route: Amsterdam to Phuket via Abu Dhabi

author: Rasa Monazzahian
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   I’ve flown with Etihad many times before and never had an issue — until now. I booked a ticket from Phuket to Yerevan through a third-party site. At no point during booking or online check-in did it mention that checked baggage wasn’t included. No baggage option appeared at check-in either. I’ve traveled with Etihad just last month to London with a 30kg baggage allowance. So imagine my shock when I arrive at Phuket airport and they tell me I have to pay $370 for a 15kg bag.  After arguing for 30 minutes, the check-in staff finally said, “I’ll help you — go buy a small bag and remove 7kg, then I’ll charge you 4,000 baht for the rest.” So I did exactly that. I bought a hand luggage bag, took the time to reorganize my stuff, and came back. Then the same staff member changes his mind and says he “no longer wants to help me” because I had previously argued with him. And now I have to pay another $260, even after buying a bag and removing weight! In the end, my one-way ticket with only 8kg of checked baggage cost me over $1,100. Unbelievable. Etihad used to be a decent airline, but this was disgusting customer service and absolutely unprofessional behavior. There was no transparency, no help, and no respect. I will never fly with Etihad again and will warn everyone I know to avoid them.
route: Phuket to Yerevan via Abu Dhabi

author: Ivo Lojda
review_text: Not Verified | The worst experience. I bought flights from Vienna to Male. We missed flight from Vienna because of crazy traffic. When we came to airport the check in was closed. No possibility to contact Etihad-airways via App the chat couldn't contact you with operators. We bought new tickets and fly to Male. When we wanted to make check-in back, we never been able to find our reservation. After 4 (four!) hours we contacted operator and they told us, that our flight back was declined via Etihad-airways because we didn't use first flight to Male. If we wanted to use our flights tickets back we should have to buy twice value more than we paid in advance. Pay
route: Vienna to Male via Abu Dhabi

author: R Barter
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Flights were fine, customer service team are terrible. I recently flew business class return from Bangkok to London via Abu Dhabi. On my return to Bangkok I realised my new suitcase had been damaged during the flight. I was in my hotel in Bangkok opening my case when I saw the damage. I took photographs of the damage, boarding pass, suitcase with baggage receipts attached, baggage tag receipts all attached to boarding pass. I contacted the Etihad help desk in Bangkok who told me to file a complaint online regarding the baggage damage which I duly did. I heard nothing from Etihad customer service for a week so I followed up. I shortly after received a reply saying my damage claim could not be proceeded because I did not take a photo of the case with the long airline baggage tag attached even though I did provide photos of the bag tag receipts attached to the suitcase. The attitude of the customer service staff was you haven’t claimed correctly so tough. It was very obvious that my suitcase was damaged while in their care but they had found an excuse not to take responsibility. No customer service shown at all. It is a misnomer to call them “customer service staff” because the last thing they want to do is provide customer service! I was made to feel like I was the one trying to make a fraudulent claim. I had spent thousands of dollars for these flights but when I came to claim a mere $100 for an obviously damaged suitcase in their care they used a technicality to refuse the claim.
route: London to Bangkok via Abu Dhabi

author: Adrian Pritchard
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   I had an entire row to myself, the leg room was generous. Food was good despite the quantity not being overly spectacular. It was a fairly short flight (6 hours) and only one round was made of the cabin. The crew were friendly. My only gripe, the IFE, yes there were loads of options, but it was nearly all American rubbish! Very little if any UK or Aussie content.

author: F Hamer
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   One hour delay in Cairo followed by 5 hour delay in AUH. Estimated arrival time in Tokyo pushed out by 6 hours. On-time record of this airline is bad.

author: G Devere
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   I recently traveled with Etihad, and it was the worst and most stressful experience I’ve ever had with an airline. My total journey from Seoul to Barcelona increased from the planned 20 hours to over 30 hours due to a cancellation. What made this experience even more frustrating was the complete lack of support and communication from Etihad staff. I had to find my way to Terminal 2 and re‑check in for a new flight completely on my own — an ordeal that almost caused me to miss the connection, if not for the help of Korean airport staff, despite their limited English. I had paid €13 for a window seat, only to be assigned a completely different seat on a different aircraft. No one contacted me to warn about the change or offered any kind of apology. I understand that a flight cancellation caused by a bird strike is beyond the airline’s control. However, it is Etihad’s responsibility to minimize the disruption, support its passengers, and acknowledge the impact caused by such significant delays. In this case, that didn’t happen. I lost an entire workday and had to rearrange critical personal commitments because of this mishandled situation. I’ve taken hundreds of flights in my life, and this was by far the worst and most stressful experience I’ve ever had. Etihad has been the biggest disappointment I’ve ever encountered with an airline. If you’re considering flying with Etihad, be aware that when things go wrong, their support and accountability may be nowhere to be found.
route: Bangkok to Barcelona via Abu Dhabi

author: Sam Burton
review_text: Not Verified |  Etihad still waiting on that refund taking over a month. Have contacted your help line 5 times in that time and been given told 5 days will get the refund. For content Etihad cancelled the flight 10 days out from the flight which was a transit flight. The help desk has been shocking to deal with for the refund. I would not fly them or personally book with them again out of principle. Can’t comment on the flight Qatar Airways we flew with eventually after a 20 hour layover over though was pretty exceptional
route: Shanghai to Rome via Abu Dhabi

author: William Stephen Jackson
review_text: Not Verified |  I was denied boarding in error as I was told at the gate in Kuala Lumpur that I needed a visa to enter Vietnam. As the holder of a UK passport I do not need a visa. I have had many emails back and forth to Etihad with the usual standard replies. Yesterday I emailed them and included this text "pursuant to the Vietnam Government's Resolution No.128/NQ-CP dated on August 14, 2023. Visa exemption will be applied to nationals of The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland with a maximum temporary residence period of 45 days from the date of entry". Their reply to me is: "After reviewing your case, I must inform you that it does not qualify for compensation or reimbursement. I understand this may not be the response you were hoping for, and I truly empathize with the difficulties you faced during your travel. We have fully reviewed your case and fairly addressed all your concerns. As our position remains unchanged, respectfully, we now consider this case closed." Case closed and no compensation for the 800 dollars extra I had to pay. I tried calling them this morning and was advised to open the case again (and waste another three months!)
route: Barcelona to Da Nang via Abu Dhabi

author: P Kersten
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Average Airline with poor booking process and poor mobile App. I am mostly facing issues with the booking process. The IOS App hangs, the website sometimes aswell. Last time the payment failed maybe because I am booking the trip starting from another country then I am currently located. The customer service is never available, you're stuck forever either on the hotline or waiting in that useless online chat. The flight itself is mostly average. For the price it's just OK. Cleanlyness of the cabin sould sometimes be a bit better. If you not choose the most expensive economy ticket, then you need to pay (hefty amounts) for any seat selection. Meals are not bad. But mostly they run out of the meal that I would choose.

author: N. Siotto
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   This was a return flight. My outbound trip was three days earlier with a nineteen years old B777. The difference was night and day.  The service was exceptional. The food comparable to fine dining in a restaurant. The seat was very comfortable with a massage option. Toilets were spacious and clean. WiFi was fast and reliable throughout the flight and quite reasonably priced. Approx 10$ for unlimited data for the full flight. The seat experience on their B787 in my opinion is among the best. Etihad became my first choice departing from the United Arab Emirates.

author: Luca Anselmi
review_text: Not Verified |  Etihad has become unreliable. I paid for an Etihad flight and was shocked to board an old Wamos Air aircraft instead. The plane was outdated, uncomfortable, and reminded me of Wizzair at its worst. Customer service was nonexistent. This is unacceptable for a premium airline. No wi fi. Zero entertainment

author: Eric Gottwald
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   We were due fly to Singapore on Dec 28th 2024 with 4 people. One person fell ill, so we had to cancel the flights. Since Dec 29th 2024, I have been trying now to get the ticket costs (minus the cancellation fee of 40%) back from Etihad Airways. Despite 8 times phone calls and several emails that the costs will be refunded after a processing time of 40 days, nothing has happened to date (6 months later).
route: Frankfurt to Singapore via Abu Dhabi

author: Suhaib Hammad
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |    Baggage policy is the worst. 7KG, who can fit stuff for 7 nights in a 7 kg bag. We got charged $76 for 5kg even though we were over by 2kg from our duty free items we bought.
route: Amman to Male via Abu Dhabi

author: Mattijs de Jager
review_text: Not Verified |  This was the worst experience I've had with an airline. First, they charge outrageous fees for just 5 or 10 kilos of extra luggage. Second, I purchased two tickets and reserved two seats to have extra space, but the second seat was simply resold because the passenger name didn’t check in — even though I paid for it. Etihad took weeks to respond, only to say this is their policy. I fly often, but never again with Etihad. My friends and family won’t either.
route: Bangkok to Amsterdam via Abu Dhabi

author: Chris Sansom
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Excellent flights with Etihad, flying Colombo to Abu Dhabi on A320 had emergency exit row on red eye flight with very good service and comfort. Smooth connection at Abu Dhabi and then EY 65 to London Heathrow on 22/5 flying the B789. This flight was superb sat in 37C at the rear of the aircraft spacious and comfortable as only 2 seats. The Cabin Crew provided great hospitality with several drink runs and tasty meals and I would like to recognise Anil, Kate ,Disha and Victoria for exceptional service. Thank you Etihad.
route: Colombo to London Heathrow via Abu Dhabi

author: Piriyanka Jeyalingam
review_text: Not Verified |  Etihad advertises itself as a premium airline – but the only “premium” thing about my experience was the level of disappointment. On my flight from Frankfurt to Shanghai (March 28 – April 17, 2025), my baggage was severely delayed (business trip). Etihad didn’t respond until an entire month later, offering either a voucher or a bank transfer as compensation. I accepted neither of these options. Before my return flight from Bangkok to Frankfurt on May 22, 2025, I submitted an upgrade request as a goodwill gesture in light of the previous incident. I reached out via three emails and two live chats (each with over 1 hour wait time). No one ever responded. The assigned case officer? Silent. Etihad’s strategy is clear: delay until the customer gives up. To make matters worse, my ticket was marked “upgrade eligible”. But at the check-in counter and gate, I was told: An upgrade would cost €1,000 per person per leg. No goodwill. No apology. No acknowledgment of the ongoing unresolved issue.  Etihad looks good on paper – but once there’s a problem, they disappear. No accountability. No service. No respect for their passengers.
route: Frankfurt to Bangkok via Abi Dhabi

author: Joseph Murray
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Our original booking was Economy but we bid for an upgrade to business class and were successful. Firstly, at check in my wife and I were assigned seats in different parts of the cabin, in rows 5 and 11. We only noticed this when we boarded the aircraft. A gentleman who was traveling unaccompanied kindly volunteered to move so that we could sit beside each other. The seat adjustment on my seat (5E) did not work. I was unable to recline the seat to sleep, which was our primary reason for purchasing the upgrade. I brought the problem to the attention of the chief stewardess after take-off and she too was unable to adjust the seat. She subsequently advised that the seat had already been logged as faulty "on the system". She was unable to offer me another seat as the business class cabin was full. As a result, I spent the journey with the seat stuck in a 90 degree upright position and disembarked with a sore back. It is mind boggling that Etihad would assign a seat which they knew to be faulty to a business class passenger. I lodged complaint with customer service and requested a refund of the additional upgrade cost for one seat. Their response stated “Our records indicate that the seat was logged as faulty, and the information was not communicated to you prior to your boarding. We acknowledge the issue this caused, especially since the business class cabin was fully booked, preventing us from offering an alternative seat“. It contained further glib comments such as “We value your loyalty and past positive experiences with Etihad. Your feedback is crucial in helping us maintain and enhance the quality of our services”. But no compensation was offered, despite a number of follow up emails from me. We are senior citizens who travel frequently, but never again with Etihad.

author: Kate Kouzoupi
review_text: Not Verified |  I recently booked two long-haul Economy Class tickets with Etihad from Athens to the Philippines and was very disappointed with the updated cabin baggage policy. Etihad now only allows one cabin bag of up to 7kg, with no personal item allowed (such as a backpack, small handbag, or even a duty-free bag).
route: Athens to Manila via Abu Dabi

author: B Parwas
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   The worst business class experience in September 2024. The business class sitting arrangement in the first flight was two rows of 2x2. The legroom between two rows was inadequate; when the front row seat was leaned, it became difficult for the backseat person to walk out of the seat comfortably. The backrest of back row seat did not lean enough because of the separator wall behind it. The leg-rest was very awkward and uncomfortable; the leg-rest inclined up a little, about 15-20 degrees, and it did not support the legs to have a proper rest. The food served was economy class standard. The crew members were busy chatting among themselves the whole time. There was no power point in the business class seat. I had two hours to go through security check and a long walk to catch the next flight. At Abu Dhabi airport, I requested for electric cart to move but was denied. The second flight of my journey was very long (nearly 15 hours) and I hoped to work and also to have a proper rest with flat seats.  The power points of my seat were not working and so I had to get my laptop charged from another seat.  After I woke up, when I asked for breakfast, I was told that my breakfast, which I selected at the beginning of the flight, was not available anymore.
route: Kolkata to Chicago via Abu Dhabi

author: William Stephen Jackson
review_text: Not Verified | I am discovering that Etihad Airways has no customer service whatsoever. I have a grievance with them over denied boarding on the last leg of my flight to Da Nang which was with their partner airline Batk Air. The flight was on one ticket contracted with and paid to Etihad Airways. I was denied boarding in Kuala Lumpur at the gate as the staff stated that I needed a visa to enter Vietnam. As a British passport holder I do not need a visa to enter Vietnam for a stay of up to 45 days. As there was no way to convince them of this and I did not want to miss the flight I contracted an online visa at a cost of 320 dollars, but was too late to board. I then had to go through immigation in Kuala Lumpur (lovely, helpful staff) and was then completely on my own. The only routing I could find on the same day was to fly to Ho Chi Minh city and then on to Da Nang; both flights I had to pay for. On arrival to Vietnam at immigration I was told that I did not need a visa and this is also clearly explained on the Vietnamese government's website. I have been in communication with Etihad Airways whilst in Vietnam and since my return to Spain. They are just not interested. I keep receiving a standard reply which says in essence - tough luck, now go away-. This is appalling treatment of a paying customer when it is very clear that the error was on their part. I don't recommend this airline and will certainly never fly with them again.
route: Barcelona to Da Nang via Abu Dhabi

author: A Shahul
review_text: Not Verified | The disappointing experience with Etihad airline has left us deeply dissatisfied. My daughter, a 15-year-old, recently traveled alone on your flight from Abu Dhabi to Chennai. The flight was delayed by over 5 hours, and including the check-in and waiting time, she was at the airport for more than 8 hours. Despite the long wait and the fact that she was traveling as an unaccompanied minor, there was no proper communication, support, or even basic assistance provided. What is most disheartening is that no food or refreshments were arranged during the late-night delay. This led to considerable stress and discomfort for her, especially since she was alone and expecting some level of care from your team. She was exhausted, frustrated, and completely let down by the service and response from your staff. This was her first experience flying with Etihad Airways, and sadly, it turned out to be extremely disappointing. She mentioned that she does not wish to fly with Etihad again and will not be recommending your airline to anyone. She is also planning to share her experience publicly on Etihad’s social media channels, hoping that this might lead to better care for other young solo travelers in the future. As a parent, I trusted Etihad with the responsibility of ensuring my daughter’s comfort and safety, but the lack of support and empathy has left us upset. I will not recommend to anyone to take ETIHAD AIRWAYS.

author: Namdar Ariana
review_text: Not Verified |  I had some bags that were a couple of bags overweight. They wanted to charge me about 1200 aed which is equivalent to 450 USD for bringing 12 kg of extra weight over four bags. Their manager asked me to buy another bag and then they would only charge me 340 aed. So I bought another bag for 330 aed, and when I came back to the counter after rearranging all my belongings the manager and guy at the counter said that I have to pay 740 aed more. Imagine bringing 12 extra kg of weight over 4 bags and having to pay about 1070 aed more just for your belongings. This is by far one of the worst airline experiences I’ve ever had. Etihad policies are beyond unreasonable. Their supervisors are unhelpful. Their economy seats are even worse, as they give you no leg room. I won’t ever be flying Etihad again, and would recommend everyone around me not to either.

author: Rohith Jayawardene
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   I was booked from Singapore to London and flew on an A380 from Abu Dhabi to London. Singapore to Abu Dhabi was a red-eye flight and Abu Dhabi to London, daylight. I have always enjoyed flying on the A380s and have been able to secure forward-facing window seats, with extra storage on the side of the seat. The upper deck is for business and first class passengers. The first leg began with welcome drinks and hot towels. Although dine-on-demand is available, I think the cabin crew were keen to expect everyone to dine simultaneously. A thin soft mattress, large pillow, blanket and slippers are all provided. Seat functions, from flat-bed to seat firmness and other options are easy to control. The amenity kit is basic, nothing special. The menu offers a good selection of starters, main courses and desserts. Following a tender braised beef with sweet potato mash for the main course for dinner, I moved to the onboard lounge for a coffee and cognac. The small lounge can seat up to 6 passengers and has a self-service bar.  The second leg began from the Etihad Business Lounge in Abu Dhabi, where you can board some flights directly from the lounge.  One of the things I do enjoy flying with Etihad is their tasty meals and dining. The list of alcoholic drinks is not extensive, but they are mostly premium brands. Prior to lunch, I was treated to a White Negroni cocktail (Campari, gin and dry vermouth). For the main course, Lamb Shank with rice was one of the most delicious onboard meals I've had. While the IFE features a good selection of entertainment, my regular complaint has been the lack of new movies, as it seems to keep repeating the same old films (since I last flew with them about four months ago). Settling to watch some TV shows and documentaries, and cabin crew spoiling me with more drinks and snacks, it was an enjoyable cruise all the way to London. I have had minor criticisms in the past, and a few negative views on privacy and service on their Dreamliner, and when flying Economy. Yet in my experience, travelling in Business Class, I have come to appreciate Etihad's general standard of consistency in service and comfort. And on this trip, two great A380s in one journey felt like having two for the price of one!
route: Singapore to London via Abu Dhabi

author: William Jackson
review_text: Not Verified |  Our flight was from Barcelona to Abu Dhabi, then to Kuala Lumpur and then on to Da Nang. The flights to Kuala Lumpur were fine, a tad stingy on the food and drink, but reasonably comfortable. The major problem occurred when I was denied boarding by Etihad Airwys' partner airline Batik Air in Kuala Lumpur. The reason given was that I needed a visa to enter Vietnam. I had previously checked and double checked and knew that I did not need a visa. I showed the staff at the boarding gate proof that I did not need a visa, but they did not let me board the flight. I then organised an online visa at a cost of over 300 USD but was too late to board. At that point I was left on my own. I was told to book another flight. I had to go through immigration in Kuala Lumpur which thanks to some very helpful officials was very easy. The only route I was able to find at short notice was a flight to Ho Chi Minh city and then from there a flight to Da Nang. Malaysia Airlines asked for no evidence of a visa for my flight to Ho Chi Minh city and when I arrived there I was told I did not need a visa to enter Vietnam and was given the standard 45 days entry stamp in my passport. I then booked a flight to Da Nang and arrived eight hours later than planned after a very stressful day through no fault of mine and with an extra cost of approximately 800 euros. Etihad Airways customer service was worse than useless. The person I spoke to had two phrases in his repertoire: "I am sorry sir, I cannot help you with that sir" and " I am sorry sir, I am not authorised to deal with that sir". I emailed Etihad Airways and received a standard reply that they were very busy and might reply to me within 28 days. If not I could contact them again! On my return to Spain I telephoned customer service again to be told that they could not be held responsible for visa problems. Pointing out to them that the problem was theirs not mine was like banging my head against a brick wall. After various emails it now seems that Etihad Airways are "looking into the matter". What that really means I have no idea. Time will tell.
route: Barcelona to Kuala Lumpur via Abu Dhabi

author: C Haydir
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Despite the 5 hours duration of the flight, no proper meal was provided, only a small sandwich, which was quite insufficient. Additionally, one of the toilets onboard was out of service, leading to long queues and inconvenience throughout the flight. I chose to fly with Etihad expecting a comfortable and premium experience, not one akin to a low-cost carrier. This experience has left me quite dissatisfied and questioning my future travel choices.

author: E Latihil
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   I never imagined that flying with Etihad Airways  would result in such an emotionally exhausting and unjust experience. My checked baggage, weighing 11kg, was completely lost. After repeated follow-ups and weeks of silence, I was told I would be compensated USD 297, based on $27 per kilogram. To make matters worse, I was shocked to see that on the WorldTracer system, my baggage was falsely marked as “found.” I have never received my bag. This false status now prevents me from pursuing my case further. The airline insisted on original purchase receipts for compensation, which is not a requirement under UAE law for the statutory compensation per kilogram of lost baggage. They then told me the case was “closed,” without properly addressing these points or correcting the false baggage status. There was no empathy, no legal fairness, and no real effort to resolve the issue. If you’re flying Etihad, be warned: if something goes wrong, you may be on your own — even if you know your rights and try to pursue them. I expected better.

author: G Anu
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   I flew from Toronto to Colombo  via AUH. It's a long 14 hr flight. Flight was a new A350. Very comfortable. Service is terrible, food portions are very small and choices are available are all Indian food. No other options available. Only chicken or veg are the two options. After the dinner service no mid flight snack available. Only available option for snack is 4 small Oreo cookies. No water service, have to go to galley and get your water if you need water. Etihad has cut down their service and I felt like I flew on a north American carrier, not a middle eastern carrier. You cannot compare with Emirates or Qatar anymore.

author: David Houlihan
review_text: Not Verified |  Return to BKK - Business Class flights both on time. Ground crew have the customer care skills second to a Military sergeant, rude, disengaged and flippant. Seats requested were honored. Plane was clean and was quite smooth. Food below expectations, menus are now clearly on the cost cutting plan. Soup / Chicken thighs and ice cream or cheese. Wines like others have mentioned are low quality. Champagne is worth avoiding and not palatable. Last but not least the cabin Crew obviously do the very basics are not proactive and had to be called each time. Too busy sitting and chatting in the galley than ensuring any passenger may want something. A very disengaged attitude and lacked any polish or personal engagement skills. Robotic

author: Mincy Kurian
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   The customer service was extremely poor. They charged me for a stopover and booked a hotel near the airport without informing me that a transit visa was required to reach it. Even the hotel booking confirmation email lacked this crucial detail. Since it was our first time traveling through Abu Dhabi Airport, we assumed the hotel was inside the airport. The response from the Etihad booking team was terrible, and their service was disappointing.  Essentially, they charge you for the stopover, book the ticket, and then mark you as a no-show at the hotel, ultimately scamming you.
route: Melbourne to Kuwait via Abu Dhabi

author: Kim Thomsen
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | Please note booking was made directly with Etihad. Trip started great with a visit to Etihad's excellent lounge at Term 4 at LHR. It became time for boarding and it was clear the flight was going to be delayed. Etihad ground staff did their best to keep us informed and they had a large number of staff at the gate to answer questions. We were assured that any missed connections would be dealt with in AUH and we departed about 2 hours late. The A380 is as always an excellent plane and the seat and staff were to match on this flight. Etihad offers dine on demand and I opted for a sandwich prior to landing in order to get some sleep. I did connection to the wifi prior to getting some rest and about 45 minutes after take off I received an email stating I had been rebooked to a later flight from AUH to BKK. I was able to accept the rebooking and get my boarding pass within an hour of taking off from LHR. The seat is excellent both for sitting/lounging and sleeping. Staff were on the ball and offered me food as soon as I woke up. At AUH ground staff were waiting for us with a number of counters set up with pre-printed boarding cards for passengers with missed connections. All you had to do was go to the right counter and get your onwards boarding card. I skipped all that and went straight to the impressive business class lounge at AUH and spent a few hours there before my connecting flight. A B777 took me the last leg to BKK. The seat consistency Etihad has across their wide body fleet is impressive and gives a familiar feel regardless of the aircraft type. Once again staff were excellent. The only downside I could find on this flight was they have cut the pre-landing snack service, but the flight is relatively short so not a massive issue. Overall a very enjoyable flight despite arriving at my destination about 4 hours later than expected, but I wish all airlines would handle delays that well, big praise to Etihad on this one. The only place they have fallen down a bit is they have not proactively offered me compensation as I am intitled to and finding that on their website is not straight forward, however once the process is started it is very quick and easy.
route: London Heathrow to Bangkok via Abu Dhabi

author: Suhail Kazim
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   The entire flight there was no wifi and the staff took turns informing us it would start in a few minutes, until one staff finally admitted there would be no wifi due to technical issues.  The staff were nice but did not know their job. The shower was also not working and no one bothered to inform the premium first-class passengers. The lesser said of their IFE, the better. They are proud to keep 6-7 games. The icing on the cake comes from the disgusting level of customer service which Etihad is now gaining laurels for. First-class service involves much more precision than serving caviar and with this level of customer service, get ready for the decline of Etihad.

author: Kamran Hussein
review_text: Not Verified |  Our Family holiday to from Heathrow to the Maldives via Abu Dhabi. The plane departure from Heathrow was delayed by a couple of hours. It was a long flight the the entertainment systems was not working. Then from Abu Dhabi there was a 15hr delay. Eventually got to the resort a day late. Not great experience and still waiting for compensation from Etihad after 6 months.
route: Heathrow to Maldives via Abu Dhabi

author: Jean-Claude Albrecht
review_text: Not Verified |  I did not pay attention that my ticket did not include a suitcase, at check in I was asked to pay £200 for my suitcase of 7 Kg. Airlines are good at sending their customers to the competition. Wont see me ever again.

author: Debora Bandeira
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   We had two flights with Etihad last week. Phuket - Abu Dhabi - Dublin. The first flight was an hour late to take off. I mean after everyone was onboard and everything seemed ready, we still waited almost an hour to take off. In both flights, the staff looked and spoke to people as if they were doing us a favor.  Beef option offered, minced meat given. Very cheap for a company that sell themselves as a premium airline. And it was a flight from Thailand, where minced beef is not even a common thing in their culinary. The only positive thing I can say about the flights was the comfortable seat recline. But overall, they are far behind Emirates and Qatar Airways service quality. That’s for sure!
route: Phuket to Dublin via Abu Dhabi

author: R Kellen
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Flying from Pakistan to Denmark. Not able to continue my travel from Abu Dhabi because the plane was overbooked. Customer service is out the window. They’re not following rules and regulation. The regulation for compensation is actually on their own webpage, but they are not following them. Now I’m lying in bed at an airport hotel with three meal vouchers and waiting 24 hours to continue my journey. And the compensation is a $300 voucher that can only be used for transportation within Etihad Airways. It feels like a joke when you receive a voucher. I couldn’t believe my eyes. Normally I travel Qatar/Emirates when I’m travelling in this region. This is just a reminder why?

author: Phil Kelly
review_text: Not Verified |  Tickets were bought at a great price. Outbound and return flights were on time and arrived at destination early. Seat was OK, we were in the rear of the aircraft, so reclined further than normal. Food was tolerable (it's Economy). Cabin crew were terrible, not one smile, grudging service - requests for water were ignored. One male FA in particular was bordering on hostile. I'd fly Etihad again, if I had to.
route: London to Melbourne via Abu Dhabi

author: M Taylor
review_text: Not Verified | The worst flight experience I’ve ever encountered. The seat armrest had collapsed and the reclining mechanism was broken meaning the seat continually slid forward and back for the entire 4.5 hour flight. The seat was covered in stains. The discomfort on the entire journey was made worse when I took the issue up with customer care afterwards. I just got a generic sorry and they closed the case, unwilling to do anything to rectify the situation or encourage me to fly with them again. I actually couldn’t believe that a legacy carrier can have such a lack of aftercare. They just want the money and don’t care about repeat business. Never use them again.

author: D Casse
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   On our flight we did not receive any drinks (sparkling water could not be provided pre take-off). When asked about food, we confirmed our order, and re-ordered drinks. Still drinks did not arrive. After 2.5 hours of waiting for any drink or food I decided to go to sleep (it was 00:30 at this time), when the air hostess told me the food was finally ready. By that time I did not feel like eating anything as it was way too late (two hours after being offered food). I complained about this with Etihad - after more than a week the only response I got was to provide booking information (which I did). It is now over three weeks since my initial complaint and Etihad still has not gotten back to me. I'm appalled at the terrible service provided but what's even more galling is the complete lack of care from the customer care staff. This should have been resolved weeks ago but Etihad simply chooses not to engage with customer complaints. Will never fly with this airline again.

author: Dennis Bacon
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | What has happened to Etihad? I was very disappointed having flown with Etihad many times. First of all, business class was rammed, high prices yet poor in flight service, food and third rate wines including being served sparking wine not champagne - other little luxuries cut back too: chocolates, cookies, basic amenity kit etc I found the service cursory, not once did I feel like a business class passenger, not once was I asked if my food, or for that matter anything else, was ok. No offer to replenish water during both long flights. The food was average, the wine dreadful! It was low cost plonk and nothing like the quality of Etihad of old. So, in summary, far less but for more money. 2 x tickets almost £6k. Etihad is not alone in fleecing customers and should work much harder to impress. They’re not alone, many airlines are making record profits whilst cutting service quality and amenity. Planes are packed, prices are sky high and there’s no quid pro quo with what’s being delivered. Even the lounges are packed, often with non business class passengers who are (understandably) taking advantage of an offer or paying extra. Trouble is, all of this dilutes the quality for business class travellers. Finally, fast track at LHR was a joke, a national embarrassment. SE Asia / Bangkok hugely more efficient. Very disappointing all round.
route: London to Bangkok via Abu Dhabi

author: Santosh Dhakal
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Very good service. There was a guy name Azad in the checkin line and he was very sincere helpful and was handling everything very professionally. He was helping me with every details and he was trying helping and giving his help to everyone. The flight experience is very good too. The seats were very comfortable and monitor works very good. Food was good too. Hopefully i will travel with eithad soon and will have a chance to meet this hospitality again.

author: Rohith Jayawardene
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | I was not exactly looking forward to two long haul flights to London, especially departing at 2.15 in the morning, and with a 4 hour layover in Abu Dhabi. However, the check-in was smooth, but there was a delay in the incoming aircraft, so we actually departed an hour later. I had booked and paid for extra leg room seats (nearer the front of the aircraft) for both flights. Having 3 inches more leg room did make a difference in comfort. At the seat was placed a pillow and blanket, along with headphones. There was also a very basic amenity kit that just had an eye mask, ear plugs and hand lotion. The pouch itself opens up to a small bag. The meal service on both flights was pretty bland. I also observed that on recent Economy Class flights, the alchoholic drinks served is rather meagre. The wine in the small paper cup was only half full. On one occasion, when I requested whiskey, I felt embarrassed to have no more than a tablespoon served - just enough for one sip! Overall, despite my opinion about the food and drinks, the flights were comfortable. I was even able to doze off for a couple of hours on both flights.
route: Bangkok to London Heathrow via Abu Dhabi

author: N Bardena
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   I had the worst flying experience with Etihad Airways at Abu Dhabi International Airport. I arrived at the airport 1 hour and 40 minutes before my flight to Boston. After waiting in a poorly managed check-in line (where other passengers were allowed to cut in front), I was informed that U.S. citizens must arrive over two hours early, a policy that was never mentioned during booking or on my ticket. The staff was completely unhelpful. I was sent back and forth between the check-in desk and ticket counter for over 30 minutes while my flight boarded. I was then told I could only rebook for the next day at an outrageous cost of $700, with no other options offered, no accommodation, no food vouchers. Etihad’s lack of clarity on policies, dismissive staff, and poor management made this an unbelievably stressful experience. I do not recommend flying with Etihad Airways unless you want to risk being stranded at the airport with no support and forced to pay exorbitant fees.

author: David Houlihan
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   As the saying goes fool me twice more fool me ! Etihad appears to now take this as its vision . Flights to in business to Nairobi cancelled last September by them as they cut the route - no explanation - we had to follow up constantly and after months got rebooked onto a flight due to leave today. Applied for Kenyan visa well in advance - one was received the travelling partners was not and frantic trying to get an update. 2 hours to departure still no visa and called Etihad to explain (realise completely it’s not their fault ) but the reply is not our problem . Yes correct - I asked to move the dates - told no - (lies). I asked if they refuse to do so what is the refund policy - (don’t know) Asked had they any idea of what is the policy  we’ll email the team and let you know! Wonderful customer care yet again 13 years as a gold member - ok this is what your offering as service ? Well I have choices - keep your greedy hands on every dime and knickle. Short term money grab strategy

author: Istimraj Paras
review_text: Not Verified |  I had an extremely frustrating experience with this airline, primarily due to their app and help desk. Trying to get any assistance through the app is next to impossible. The interface is confusing, and when you finally manage to get in touch with customer support, the responses are vague, unhelpful, and often seem automated or like a scam. I encountered multiple issues during my booking process, and when I tried to resolve them through the help desk, no one seemed capable of offering a real solution. It felt like they were deliberately avoiding responsibility, and after a lot of back-and-forth, I still had no clear answers. This airline clearly does not prioritize customer service or transparency, and I highly advise against using them. The lack of proper support and the overall negative experience left me completely dissatisfied.
route: Islamabad to New York via Abu Dhabi

author: N Siotto
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   With a small fee it’s possible to upgrade to Economy Space which is close to Premium Economy space. Compared to Economy Basic the seat has substantially more legroom and slightly more reclining. The food was delicious given the class of travel. Toilets clean. Etihad is now my priority when possible.

author: Nash Degaonkar
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified |   Etihad has a good economy, and I sat on the A350-1000 from ORD to AUH, and with A380 from AUH to BOM. Seat comfort on the A350 made me feel like I was on the driver's seat of my BMW. Food was better on the first leg of the flight, and could have been better on the second. However, on the A350, there were no plugs provided, so could not charge laptop. That is what Etihad needs to look at for once.
route: Chicago to Mumbai via Abu Dhabi

author: S Albarn
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | My experience with Etihad Airways was extremely disappointing and far below the expectations for an airline of this calibre. First, I was informed just a few hours before landing in Abu Dhabi that all hotels participating in the stopover programme were fully booked. This forced me to find last-minute accommodation at a much higher cost, with the risk of not finding availability. Despite several attempts to contact the company, I received no response, highlighting a severe lack of professionalism and customer care. Additionally, the flights themselves were equally frustrating. Both on the Lisbon to Abu Dhabi and Abu Dhabi to Bali routes, the seat space was extremely cramped, making the journey very uncomfortable, especially for long-haul flights. The food served on all legs of the trip was of very low quality, far below that offered by other airlines operating hubs like Doha or Dubai.
